News.title: At least 50 injured after fireworks ‘explode into crowd’ at packed festival in Spain as panicked crowd flees
News.content:
AT least 50 people have been injured after multiple fireworks exploded into a packed square in Spain.

At around midday, horror blasts suddenly rocked through the Plaza de los Fueros sending revelers fleeing in fear.



Dozens of people had gathered in Noáin to celebrate the start of the town’s annual patron saint festivities when the panic unfolded.

A municipal employee had been cradling a bundle of fireworks on the town hall balcony when all of them suddenly exploded, according to Luis Maya, Councilor for Citizen Security.



Maya said: “Among so many people, I don’t know if it was due to carelessness or a shove , but all the rockets ignited at once with their fuses.”

At least three rogue fireworks ricocheted into the crowd while others exploded on the Town Hall balcony.



Shocking footage shows smoke pouring out of a building while large crowds – including children – run for cover.

Firefighters, police officers and two ambulances raced to the scene to treat the injured.

Three men in their 40s and 50s have been rushed to the University Hospital of Navarra with burns to their hands and feet.

One of the three men – aged 41, 53 and 54 – was the employee carrying the fireworks on the balcony.



Noain health centre has also treated 47 people with minor burns, bruises and earache, according to news outlet El Mundo.

A young girl was among those transferred to the Noain health center.

Eyewitnesses told local papers that for several seconds the only thing they could see was smoke as the roar of rockets deafened their ears.



Dramatic photos show children sprinting through the streets while covering their ears.

The town’s mayor Mikel Navarro told Spanish news site Cope: “It was scary, really scary. The first rocket went off normally, but the second one got out of control.”

“We had to set up a small field hospital to treat all the injured,” he added.

The cause of the blast is still unknown, and the Civil Guard have launched a probe into the incident.

Initial investigations suggest that the first two rockets firing off had set ablaze the stash of remaining fireworks.



The mayor praised the rapid response of the emergency crews and the City Council thanked them for their for their “quick and effective action”.

Navarro confirmed: “It now seems that everything is under control, and we hope the festivities can continue as normal, which is what we want.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The fireworks display was the first in a series of celebrations in honour of San Miguel, the patron saint of Noain.

Held every year, the festivities run from August 26 to August 30.

News.title: Lawyer accused of vile sex acts with pet dog after ‘wife caught him on security cam’ as mugshot shows bite on his nose
News.content:
BESTIALITY SHOCK Lawyer accused of vile sex acts with pet dog after ‘wife caught him on security cam’ as mugshot shows bite on his nose

A LAWYER has allegedly been caught on camera sexually abusing their family dog, his wife has claimed.

Steven Swain, 56, is slapped with bestiality charges after his wife claimed she recorded his depraved acts against her beloved pooch.



While rewatching footage recorded on November 21, 2025, she found her husband “forcing oral from their dog”, according to a probable cause affidavit.

Court filings have identified that the “small black dog” is called Shipley.



The Houston Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals contacted Detective Natalie Spellman, an animal cruelty investigator, to look into the wife’s complaint against her husband on 11 May, 2026.

The footage allegedly shows the attorney “lying on his back in a bed in a room that appeared to be a bedroom”, according to Detective Spellman.



She also recalled that you can hear Swain saying “Come here, Shipley”, with the dog eventually entering the frame.

The police mugshot shows a bite on Swain’s nose.

After discovering his depraved acts, Swain’s wife separated from him and even took the dog with her, according to court documents.

She stated that she was “unaware how long this has been going on but believes it’s happened more than once”, according to court documents.



The reason he gave to the detective why she had decided to fit extra cameras in the house was because Swain was allegedly “seeing prostitutes regularly multiple times along with other weird occurrences inside the home” between the end of October and the beginning of November 2025.

She later told detectives that she didn’t know what to do with the discovered footage, but she was “100 per cent sure” that the man defiling her dog Shipley was her husband.

Following investigations, Swain was charged with bestiality and has been released from jail on a $75,000 bond.

Swain has been practicing as an attorney in Houston since 1997.

On the website The Swain Law Firm, it says that Swain has “earned the reputation amongst his colleagues as a skilful negotiator and navigator through the courts in all matters related to probate.”



The Sun has reached out to The Swain Law Firm for comment.

News.title: Warning over ‘drunk’ wasps gorging on rotten fruit and going on stinging rampages in UK beauty spot
News.content:
SWARMS of aggressive and “drunk” wasps have been terrorising a UK beauty spot with residents urged to “watch out”.

The stinging insects were found to be feasting on fermenting fruit in the area.

The British Pest Control Association (BPCA) has warned families in East Riding to avoid disturbing wasps and their nests – as the drunken insects are more likely to attack.



Worker wasps in the area were found to be eating fermented fruit, causing them to become inebriated and more aggressive.



As a result, Natalie Bungay, head of membership and technical at BPCA, said: “Like bees and hornets, wasps are pollinators and, where possible, are best left alone.”

Instead, she advised that locals who may come across a wasp nest in a high-traffic area should assess whether it may need to be removed, and if so, to contact a BPCA member for support.

Drunken wasps are a known phenomenon in the late summer, where the sugar-hungry pests seek out rotten produce to feast on.

Bungay said: “This happens when the queen stops producing eggs and the workforce has nothing to do other than look for fermented fruits and sugars.

“Wasps quickly get inebriated and this is typically when you can expect them to be more aggressive and likely to sting.”

The elderly and young children tend to be more at risk from these angry insects – with more potential complications stemming from the stings and anaphylaxis, a life-threatening allergic reaction.

Residents have been told to dispose of rubbish properly, especially food with a high sugar content, to limit encounters with the drunken beings.



They have also been reminded that it’s important not to bat or swipe away at the wasps, as this tends to antagonise them even more.

This comes after drunk seagulls caused traffic chaos in Lowestoft and Aldeburgh, as a result of munching on swarms of flying ants.

The woozy gulls were spotted “stumbling” around and staggering into the road, particularly in Suffolk coastal towns.

News.title: I dated baby killer Jamie Varley at uni – from fake suicide to vile rage… I wish I stopped him before he could adopt tot
News.content:
FOR two years, a young boyfriend of evil Jamie Varley suffered a shocking campaign of mental and physical violence.

Charmed at first by the trainee teacher, he found himself being humiliated, beaten and controlled – and in his weakened state, he never felt able to call the police.



Now the ex, who we are calling Adam to protect his identity, spoke of his trauma and regret – and he says he fears if he had sounded the alarm on Varley’s behaviour all those years ago then Preston Davey, the little boy adopted and later murdered by deranged Varley, could be alive today.

And our exclusive pictures show Varley looking fresh-faced during his time studying at Manchester Metropolitan University between 2011 and 2013.

Adam says: “My friends used to say to me ‘One day you’re going to have an argument and he’s going to stab you’.



“And I used to laugh, and I think nowadays, I wish I had taken it more seriously.

“I excused his behaviour and accepted his apologies but I look back on it now and think, ‘What on earth was I doing? Why did I ever put up with that?’

“I feel like in the times he was acting like a complete nutcase if I had blown the whistle on him and he had any sort of formal recognition about his behaviour like a police record or something, maybe that would have prevented him from being in a position to adopt.



“So I kind of feel like I should have done something.

“But it’s much easier to think that with hindsight. I was manipulated by him and so were lots of other people and professionals.”

Varley, 37, was handed a whole life term in June after being convicted of the murder and sexual abuse of tragic Preston, who he killed just four months after adopting him in April 2023.



But more than a decade before that, he met Adam while the pair were studying and fell for him.

But Adam reveals that behind the image, the textiles teacher frequently exhibited his “Jekyll and Hyde” character and lost control any time he couldn’t get his own way.

During one row, Varley threw a mobile phone at Adam’s head and ripped a gold chain off his neck with such force that a decade later he still has a mark from it.

Adam also told how Varley once broke into his flat to argue with him and smashed up a watch when he realised it was a gift from his former partner.

Varley also once faked a suicide attempt following an explosive argument over eating a prawn during a meal and lay down in the road to prevent Adam from driving away after he ended the relationship.



Varley met Adam online and they went out for a drink in January 2011, with the “charismatic” trainee teacher charming him with his sense of humour and banter.

The pair began dating and shared a love of horror films, eating out and trips to the beach.

Varley also impressed Adam with his love for his family and doted on his nieces and nephews.



But Adam quickly realised that while Varley had a “flamboyant and fun side”, his demeanour would quickly change and become aggressive if he didn’t get attention or his own way.

On occasion, Varley would also show a violent tendency including one night when the pair were out in Manchester’s gay area.

They bumped into a former partner of Adam, who said that he noticed he was still wearing a watch he gifted him.

He recalls: “Jamie’s mood shifted and started to become very defensive and jealous.

“He asked to see the watch properly. I took it off to show Jamie and his reaction in the middle of the bar was to throw it to the ground, stamp on it smashing the glass and then proceed to throw it in the canal.”



The following morning Varley apologised but also said it was justified because he had kept a token from a past relationship.

The pair continued dating despite friends worrying they had become too full on too quickly.

“On his best days he was always very popular, polite,” recalls Adam. “He was very charming. He’d always try and win people over.



“My family took a real shine to him. He would come across as someone who would do anything for anyone.

“But the worst side of him was relentlessly argumentative and hostile. He could argue all day over the most pathetic things. His main concerns were public perception and image.

Adam said after one uni exam, he told Varley he was too tired to visit him in Blackpool and would just come over to see him the following day.

Later that night when he returned to his student accommodation in Manchester’s Hulme area, Varley had driven drunk from Blackpool and climbed over a neighbour’s fence to try and break in.

“My friends and my housemates were really worried by his behaviour by this point,” Adam says.



“The argument continued and I told him he had crossed a boundary.

“He actually pinned me down against the bed and was just screaming in my face and telling me I had put on weight and was fat and ugly.

“He said something like ‘You might as well stay with me. Don’t ever leave me because no one else is going to have you’.”



Despite the abuse, the couple continued dating.

But a few weeks later, Varley also flew off the handle in a jealous fit when his mum Karen persuaded Adam to dance with her at a family wedding.

He remembers: “I got up dancing with her and he just sat there with a face like absolute thunder.

“He just did not like the fact that I wasn’t sat with him, keeping him entertained. I was giving my attention to someone else, even though it was his mother.”

Once they returned to the hotel room, Varley “exploded” and bounced a Blackberry mobile device off Adam’s forehead and snatched a metal chain off his neck, which has left him with a scar to this day.



Back at uni, Varley continued to manipulate Adam and even convinced him to see a doctor about his mental health because that was to blame for their constant arguments.

Adam says: “He really enjoyed arguing and it was absolutely exhausting”.

On another occasion, Adam and his sister went out for dinner with Varley and tried to persuade him to eat a prawn, which he didn’t like.

Varley again exploded with rage and walked off back to Adam’s parents’ home, where he told them that Adam was a “f***ing c**t”.

He stormed off to bed and when Adam went to join him, he found him on the bedroom floor surrounded by pills that he had pretended to take in a staged suicide attempt.



Adam said: “I told him to get up and stop pretending to be unconscious because the pills were all on the floor rather than inside him.”

Varley responded by getting up, screaming at Adam and going to sleep in another room.

The relationship began to break down and the pair spent time apart in third year as they both left Manchester to do work placements.

Another huge row ensued on New Year’s Eve when Varley visited Adam and he told him it was over.

But Varley coerced him into continuing the relationship, even though it was flawed.

While apart, Varley created fake profiles on Facebook in the area where Adam was living in an attempt to message him and test his loyalty.

He said: “He’d flirt with me through fake profiles and then see if I’d do anything. He went to a lot of effort – the profiles had friends and everything.

“I also got messages from other people saying he had been in contact with them and asking about me.

“It was getting a bit stalky and a bit creepy.”

Adam moved back to Manchester to complete his degree and Varley got back in touch and said he had changed and persuaded him to give it one more go.



But Adam decided he’d had enough.

In November 2013, he visited Varley at the South Shore Academy in Blackpool and told him it was over.

Varley reacted by lying in the road for 30 minutes to prevent him from driving off.

Adam says: “He’s lying there on the tarmac, screaming, refusing to let me reverse the car. Eventually I got him back in the house and calmed him down and then I did leave.”

After moving out of Manchester, Adam had no further contact with Varley. Then he saw a news report saying he had been charged with Preston’s murder.



Adam says that even though he split with Varley a decade before Preston was murdered, he was left horrified, and wishes he had done more about his behaviour – in the hope that would have prevented social services from allowing him to adopt Preston.

He recalls: “I tried to find reasons that it couldn’t be the case but then I saw more articles and thought ‘Oh God, it is true’.

“And then when they started officially listing the full charges, I just feel sick because the reality kind of hit where I’m thinking there is a lot more to this. It was really daunting.”

Adam followed the trial at Preston crown court daily through media reports and said footage released of Varley lying on the floor screaming after being told Preston had died, and later appearing cold and calculated in police interviews, showed the two sides of his personality.

He adds: “Seeing Jamie on trial was surreal. It makes you question every relationship you have and what kind of a judge of character you are.



“You see two sides of him there and that’s very much how he was. Jamie’s problem has always been that he thinks he is a better actor than everyone else does.

“My husband says I have definitely won the award for the worst ex, but he’s also said it’s clear that Jamie managed to manipulate and fool an awful lot of people.

“I think prison will end badly for him and I don’t think he’ll see a full-life sentence.

“I’m not sure he would be able to cope with that anyway.”

News.title: My ultimate festival guide – from the best place to watch headliners to my Triple-B rule & why I always carry duct tape
News.content:
ALEX JAMES My ultimate festival guide – from the best place to watch headliners to my Triple-B rule & why I always carry duct tape

THERE might be no Glastonbury this year but UK festival season is still in full swing.

Alternative events such as Reading and Leeds later this month all anticipate huge crowds.



But whether you’re a first timer or veteran, taking the kids or camping with mates here Blur bassist ALEX JAMES, who’s played main stages worldwide, and for the last 15 years also run his own Big Feastival event at his Oxfordshire farm, shares his insider guide.

Big Feastival takes place Friday, August 28 to Sunday, August 30. Bigfeastival.com



FIRST FRIDAYS:

If you’re going to just one day of a three-day weekend festival, choose the opening Friday.



It’s harder to get people to take this day off work so often events will intentionally start off by putting their strongest music line up on to try to get people there early.

Plus, on the first day everyone’s up for it, the site’s all still new and fresh, and the atmosphere full of excitement and anticipation.



A day ticket is cheaper, and you’ll still soak up all the great vibes.

TAPE, TROLLEYS, TRASH BAGS:

Never go anywhere without duct tape.

You can mark a massive X on your canvas to help you find it, patch rips or welly leaks, fix anything.

Even some bands choose camping at festivals and don’t stay in hotels or tour buses.



There’re so many options, pop-up tent, pre-pitched, glamping.

But just take the bare minimum.

You’ll be so tired you’ll crash anyway.

Although everyone is different, my wife won’t go anywhere with a feather pillow, I’m happy to put my head on a rucksack.

Black bin liners aren’t glamorous but a great shout for chucking dirty, smelly stuff into.



And I don’t know what I’d do without a trolley, it’s handy for everything.

Brilliant for carting your stuff, or kids, across a field.

Ask organisers as you can sometimes hire them on site too.



SEEK THE SOUND TOWER:

My 100 percent top tip is finding the sound tower and positioning yourself there to enjoy artists on the main stage.

That’s where I always watch from.

Don’t even bother trying to get down to the front, I love a mosh pit, but you won’t see as well and might even miss stuff.

Besides festivals have big screens now, so you don’t really need to bother.



The sound tower is where the technical stuff is all happening, it’s where they are doing the lights and the audio so it’s absolutely the best place to be to experience the music.

BEANS, BOOTS, BOURBON

Everyone’s packing necessities vary but I never go on tour without my basic cowboy essentials: Beans, boots, bourbon!

For UK festivals also wellies, wipes and waterproofs, it could rain or roast, perhaps together.

Hood or hat, and SPF, and you’re prepared for anything.



Maybe a woolly too for nights, it gets colder than you think.

A head torch is handy and saves on phone battery.

Then even more wet-wipes.

You really can’t have too many.

SLEEPING LIONS:



Camping with kids is nothing to be scared of.

They absolutely love sleeping in tents, mine are happier than in a hotel.

Festivals in particular are a total breeze, kids are like dogs after a day at the beach at bedtime.

The fresh air totally whacks them out.

You never hear children up late on the campsites.



It’s the grown-ups who stay up and play up, making the most of the fact the kids are sleeping like lions.

If they wake up early just give them a towel and tell them to go and play in the showers.

Best 2026 festivals you can still get tickets for Battersea Park in Concert Head to south west London this Bank Holiday weekend to see this riverside park turned into an open-air venue, where the Royal Philharmonic Concert Orchestra will play hits from iconic bands such as ABBA, cinema and musical theatre classics, before closing off with jazz and soul from Ronnie Scott’s Jazz Orchestra and The Amy Winehouse Band celebrating 20 years of Back to Black. Reading and Leeds August bank holiday weekend sees the return of these twin festivals. Headliners this year include Charlie xcx, Dave, Raye, and Fontaines D.C. All Points East If you missed it last weekend, then fear not, because part two returns to Victoria Park in London this Friday, including performances from Tyler, The Creator, and Twenty One Pilots. Victorious Down on the south coast this weekend, the likes of Richard Ashcroft, The Black Keys, Kasabian, The Streets, and James Arthur will be performing in Portsmouth at this beautiful waterside location in Portsmouth – plus many more. Things kick off Friday and tickets are still available. Shambala This Thursday sees this independent festival kick off once more in the grounds of Kelmarsh Hall, Northamptonshire. Come to enjoy performances from Emma-Jane Thackray and Swedish legends Goat. Radio 2 in the Park The first ever edition of this festival in Scotland, there’ll be performances from Simple Minds, The Script, and James Blunt over the 11 to 13 September, as well as sets from Radio 2 DJs.

They’ll love it.

Also book in advance to save as many events, like ours, offer early bird incentives, payment plans and discounts such as under 5’s free.

CLOWNS FOR CALM:



Think of a festival as a marathon, not a sprint.

It’s often three days with lots of tired people by the end.

There’s lots of excitement, you’ve done a lot of steps.

It can be overwhelming.

There will be rows, tantrums, huffs and diva strops, and that’s just the bands!



Hang in there.

My advice here from experience; take a bit of calm time out, find a quiet corner, perhaps sit on a hay bale, or watch some clowns.

Headliners are typically on around 9.30pm-ish in the UK, which whether you’re playing on stage or watching it, is a long day.

Don’t be afraid to take a tactical afternoon nap.

COLD PLUNGE AND CARRY ON:



When we started Big Feastival no-one else was doing decent festival food, it was all burgers or hot dogs.

You get everything now.

Taking supplies yourself remains a balance between overpacking and running out.

But remember now there’s often a supermarket on site for essentials.

There’s still nothing like a cold beer and a live band.



But if you wake up with a sore head you won’t be the only one suffering.

Pack paracetamol, a shower – another top tip is get up early, or sleep very late, to avoid busiest times for bogs and washing – then find good coffee, or Bloody Marys.

A pay-as-you-go cold plunge or sauna is another top festival hangover reviver.

Ask where they are, they might be tucked away, but many will offer this.

POKE ABOUT:



I like being a man with a plan but as host, if I’ve done any job properly the thing you’ll enjoy the most isn’t the reason you came.

Headline acts may make you buy the ticket, but they often aren’t the highlight you leave with.

It’s actually pretty easy to book bands but I know that watching one artist you love won’t sustain a whole weekend.

Good organisers ensure variety and loads of other quirky, interesting stuff happening too.

Find smaller music sets, discover new bands, visit the silent disco, poke your head into random marquees, explore, get lost, keep an open mind.



You never know what will end up being your magical moment.

Enjoy everything.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hosting a festival truly is the most fun I’ve ever had.

The memories last a lifetime.

News.title: Shocking moment woman attacked and dog kicked in head by young yobs outside Morrisons in town centre – as three arrested
News.content:
THIS is the moment young yobs attacked a woman and her dog outside a town centre supermarket.

The thugs can be seen hitting the woman and appear to boot her dog in the head while jeering and swearing.



The assault unfolded in Newhaven town centre on Monday at around 8pm, according to police.

Three teens, including two girls and a boy, have since been arrested, cops added.



A heroic Morrisons‘ employee can be seen attempting to shield the victim from the onslaught of attacks by the group.

The footage appears to show a male kicking her dog in the head while the teens swear at the owner.

One female attacker is seen attempting to beat the victim over the head with an object before the staff member bravely attempts to deflect them.

The video circulating online has gained hundreds of comments from horrified users worried about the welfare of the lady and her dog.

Many praised the intervention of Morrisons’ staff member and one martial arts company has even offered the victim free self- defence lessons.

It is currently unclear how the altercation started.



Sussex Police told The Sun: “Three teenagers have been arrested following an incident in Newhaven High Street on Monday evening (24 August) around 8pm, during which it was reported a woman was assaulted and a dog was kicked.

“A 16-year-old boy from Hassocks and a 17-year-old girl from Brighton were both arrested on suspicion of common assault, assault occasioning actual bodily harm, causing unnecessary suffering to an animal and theft from a shop.

“Both have been bailed while enquiries continue.

“A 15-year-old girl from Brighton has also been arrested on suspicion of assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

“She remains in custody at this time.”



Lewes Neighbourhood Policing Inspector John Adams said: “We have taken swift action following this incident and three people have been arrested.

“Our enquiries are continuing as we work to establish the full circumstances of what happened.

“We understand the video circulating on social media may have been concerning for those who have seen it, and we would still ask anyone with information or relevant footage to contact us.”

Anyone with information or relevant footage is asked to contact police online or by calling 101, quoting serial 1438 of 24/08.

News.title: Four bodies found in 72hrs on holiday island after cop ‘falsely closed 300 missing persons cases & lied to families’
News.content:
SHOCK SCANDAL Four bodies found in 72hrs on holiday island after cop ‘falsely closed 300 missing persons cases & lied to families’

THE haunting discovery of four bodies on a holiday island has led to the arrest of a police officer who allegedly falsified missing persons records.

A police sergeant, named only as Bu, is facing accusations that he prematurely ended investigations into up to 300 missing people in South Korea and lied to grieving families about their loved ones.



The scandal has rocked the popular tourist destination of Jeju Island after four bodies were located in just 72 hours.

One of those found is believed to be 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran who had been missing for over three months.



She was found on Monday at a palm farm near her home with wounds consistent with suicide – 104 days after her family first reported her missing.

Jang’s family claimed they were told by the officer assigned to her case, Bu, 35, a few days after she vanished that she had been found safe.



He allegedly then told the victim’s boyfriend she had asked not to be put in contact with her loved ones as she wanted to escape her past life and start over again.

Bu then removed her case from the missing-person profiling system, police have alleged.

Investigators claim to have found no evidence Jang had ever spoken to police.

The body of a missing man in his 60s was then found in Jeju City on Saturday.



His family have now made similar accusations of police malpractice.

The man had gone missing on June 28 with Bu assigned to his case.

The sergeant again closed the case shortly after it was first filed and reportedly told the family the man was found “safe”.



His loved ones claimed Bu told them he didn’t “wish to disclose his location”.

The man’s son later told reporters: “We believed the police when they said my father was safe and waited, but after 51 days, what returned was his body.”

Authorities said there were no apparent signs of foul play in his death.

Two other bodies of people who were reported missing were also found over the weekend on Jeju Island sparking fears of a major scandal.

Police are yet to confirm if they believe Bu was involved in the last two missing persons cases.



Investigators are now examining nearly 300 reports handled by Bu.

Bu was arrested earlier this week with four officers in the sergeant’s chain of command also being put on administrative leave.

The cases have sparked so much scrutiny that South Korean President Lee Jae- Myung has now ordered a thorough investigation into the police’s handling of similar cases.

He even questioned cops in general saying: “The Korean people are questioning whether [the police] deserve this large power.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

South Korea‘s national police chief was also grilled by lawmakers at an emergency National Assembly hearing on Monday as he admitted “there is a fault in the system”.

News.title: Brit who claimed wife fell 200ft to her death during sex on hotel balcony ‘killed her to start new life with mistress’
News.content:
DEADLY TWIST Brit who claimed wife fell 200ft to her death during sex on hotel balcony ‘killed her to start new life with mistress’

A BRIT-GERMAN man who claimed his wife toppled 200ft over a balcony during sex has been sentenced to life in prison over her murder.

Christian M threw his wife from a 22-floor hotel window in Germany “like a garbage bag”, the judge said at his trial.

Marta M, 40, plummeted more than 200ft to her death on May 18 in 2023.



Christian wanted to “dispose of” his wife to start a new life with his mistress, according to the court verdict.



The chilling kill would enable him to dodge expensive divorce fees, a court heard.

Following his wife’s death, the suspect claimed she had fallen over the balcony railing during sex.

He then moved in with his mistress near Frankfurt, according to the court.



Cops investigated the claims for two years and eventually concluded that his story did not match the evidence at Leonardo Royal hotel in Frankfurt.

During a 20-day trial starting on April 1 possible sex scenes were re-enacted for the judge and jury.

Prosecutors claimed that internet searches showed Christian googling poisonous herbs, weapons, sedatives and inheritance law.

He also searched for tall mountains with deep crevices in Hesse and Bavaria – and towering hotels with balconies.



The day before the crime he booked a hotel room on the 22nd floor, telling his wife – who knew about the affair – that he wanted a “night of reconciliation”.

CCTV of the night shows Marta stumbling, apparently drunk.

Just 13 minutes after the pair returned to their room, hotel guests reported hearing screams of “no, no”.

Mum-of-two Marta was then discovered dead wearing only her bra and with bruises to her elbows from before the fall.

A court heard that the idea to frame her death as a tragic accident may have come from an episode of CSI in which a woman pushes a man off a balcony during sex.



He appeared to be under the belief that

The judge said: “We didn’t perceive her as wanting dirty sex, but rather as needing to sleep.”

“It would have been the perfect crime if the authorities hadn’t investigated so meticulously” they added.

Christian M has been ordered to pay £30,000 (35,000 euros) for the loss of a loved one to Marta’s mother and the two children they shared together.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The killer was silent throughout the trial and remained emotionless when the guilty verdict was read out, according to German newspaper Bild.



Christian’s defense lawyers have said that they will launch an appeal, reported RTL Hessen.

News.title: Video shows scale of flash flood hitting Nepal-Tibet border
News.content:
Video shows the moment a deadly massive flash flood and mudslide hit the Nepal-Tibet border.

At least 31 people have been killed, and hundreds of tourists are missing.

The first two video clips have been edited by the BBC with white flashes, due to the distressing content.

Other clips show bridges being torn apart by the floodwater as people run to find cover.

Follow the story live.

News.title: Rocky Horror star Tim Curry dies at 80
News.content:
English actor Tim Curry, best known for playing the outlandish Frank-N-Furter in film musical The Rocky Horror Picture Show, has died at the age of 80.

Curry first played the role on stage before the film version, which was released in 1975 and has remained a cult favourite.

The actor also played fearsome clown Pennywise in the 1990 TV version of Stephen King's It, and was Long John Silver in 1996's Muppet Treasure Island.

His other films included Annie, The Hunt for Red October and Home Alone 2, and he was nominated for three Tony Awards on Broadway.

Curry's manager confirmed the news of the actor's death to CBS, the BBC's US news partner.

News.title: Murder arrests after fire kills two including child in Middlesbrough
News.content:
Two people have been arrested on suspicion of murder after two died in a house fire including a child, police have confirmed.

The blaze in Grangetown, Middlesbrough, broke out just before 05:30 BST and also left a 48-year-old woman in hospital in a critical condition, alongside a further three people who suffered non-life threatening injuries.

Cleveland Police said the two victims were yet to be formally identified.

Two men, aged 23 and 31, have been arrested on suspicion of murder and are in police custody, the force said.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating what had happened but was "keeping an open mind and cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime at this time".

The fire happened about two miles from the A66 crash that killed five young men and two police officers on Saturday morning.

Redcar and Cleveland Local Policing Commander Supt Emily Harrison said the force was working to "establish the circumstances of exactly what has happened".

"We will have a high visibility presence in the Grangetown area and encourage anyone who has concerns, or who may have information, to approach our officers."

Patrols have been increased in the local area to "reassure the local community", the force said earlier.

News.title: Prince Harry and Meghan land in UK days after announcing move
News.content:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived back in the UK, BBC News understands.

Prince Harry, Meghan and their children Archie and Lilibet are believed to have flown into the country privately from California, and landed in Birmingham shortly before midday.

A spokesman for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex said "this is not something we would comment on".

There did not appear to be a police presence as Harry and his family left the airport, a source told the BBC.

Last week, it was reported that the couple would be relocating to the UK in August. They will not return to official duties but will live in Britain as non-working royals.

It is thought the family will base themselves at a private property outside of London in the Cotswolds area.

Archie and Lilibet have been enrolled in school and the new term is due to start next week.

The Sussexes left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year.

King Charles was told of the move earlier this month. The family visited the King at his Highgrove home in July this year, but it is understood the move was not discussed.

Before that visit, Prince Harry and Meghan had not been in the UK together since they attended the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022.

News.title: Stourbridge fires that razed 19 homes were accidental, say investigators
News.content:
Two fires that destroyed 19 homes in Stourbridge were started accidentally in fields where farming machinery was in use, according to West Midlands Fire Service.

Investigators established agricultural equipment was being used in the vicinity of fields immediately before the fires were first reported. The service would not confirm the type of machinery.

The first fire started in a field near Racecourse Lane at about 13:27 BST on 13 August, while a second began shortly afterwards in a field near Quarry Park Road.

The day after the fires the government sent out an emergency alert to millions of people across England and Wales, warning them against "any activity that could start a fire".

News.title: Inquest begins into death of Jason Arday
News.content:
An inquest has begun into the death of Jason Arday, the former University of Cambridge professor at the centre of a plagiarism row.

He was found dead at his home in London on 14 August, days after resigning from his post.

His appointment as Cambridge's youngest ever black professor at the age of 37 in 2023 was hailed at the time as a progressive moment.

Senior coroner Dr Julian Morris said on Wednesday: "The various reports have given me reason to suspect that Professor Arday died an unnatural death 12 days ago."

He told London Inner South Coroner's Court: "It therefore follows that I must open an investigation."

The Metropolitan Police said at the time that Arday's death was being treated as unexpected and was "not believed to be suspicious".

Arday was found "unresponsive" by family members at his home in Battersea, the inquest heard on Wednesday. Despite resuscitation efforts he was pronounced dead, the inquest was told.

The 41-year-old had faced allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements. He denied the claims, but admitted errors in his work.

He said controversy about his work had led to "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack".

The claims emerged after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in the professor's work.

Arday said some errors arose because of his autism, as he relied on using mimicry to make sense of information. Such scrutiny would find similar errors in work by other academics, he said.

After his death, his family issued a statement saying they were "in shock to have lost this amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son".

They added: "The campaign of misinformation was too much for Jason, who was a gentle man and who always wanted to see the best in everyone."

There have been calls for a public inquiry into media coverage surrounding the former Cambridge professor before his death.

Arday's memoir is due to be published in the UK on Thursday. The publisher, Simon & Schuster, announced on Monday that the book will be released as planned, with his family saying: "It is only right that we honour his wishes."

News.title: Rupert Grint to return to Harry Potter in Broadway play
News.content:
Harry Potter star Rupert Grint is to return to the role of Ron Weasley - playing the character as an adult in the spin-off play in New York.

Grint was first cast to play Ron in the original films at the age of 11. Now 38, he will join the cast of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child on Broadway for four months from next February.

The play catches up with Harry, Ron and Hermione as grown-ups, 19 years after the end of the events in the original books and films - with Ron and Hermione now married and sending their daughter to Hogwarts.

"Dusting off the old robes. New York - see you all in February," Grint wrote on Instagram, external.

Last November, he told BBC News he was unlikely to ever "step out" of Ron Weasley's shadow. "I'm fine with that. I think it's great," he said.

News.title: Rockstar Games breaks silence on Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks
News.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.

Clips appearing to show gameplay and cinematics from the title began appearing online last week, but the developer did not acknowledge them straight away.

In a statement, the company said the leaks had been "heartbreaking" for the team working on the sequel, and that they were "not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time".

The company apologised for the delays in releasing official updates on the highly anticipated title, but vowed to "exceed" fans' expectations in a special preview airing on Netflix this week.

When leaks first began to surface, there was some doubt as to whether they were genuine.

But as the days went on, evidence mounted to suggest they were legitimate.

Copies of clips were quickly taken down from social media sites via copyright strikes, where the owner of a work can request its removal.

And, on Friday, Rockstar's parent company Take Two Interactive launched legal proceedings regarding the leaks in a New York court.

Rockstar acknowledged players had been waiting for it to address the leaked footage, and said it was "unfortunate the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers".

It also thanked fans who sent messages of support over the past week, adding: "Your words have meant more to the team than you can imagine."

The group behind the leaks claims to be acting in the interests of players, accusing Rockstar of engaging in anti-consumer practices such as its decision not to release a disc version of GTA 6 at launch.

Not everyone is convinced, as each release of new material has invited viewers to send cryptocurrency "donations" to the user uploading them.

News.title: Nepalese authorities say 33 UK nationals missing after flash floods
News.content:
Thirty-three people from the UK are among hundreds feared missing following a deadly flash flood near the Nepal-Tibet border.

Flooding and mud slides hit the Rasuaw region in the morning on Wednesday, killing at least 95 people in Nepal and three in Tibet, according to Chinese state media.

Nepal police said 579 tourists are missing - including 466 who are foreign nationals, from 28 different countries.

The UK Foreign Office said it is working closely with Nepalese authorities "following concerning reports of British nationals who are missing" and has encouraged Brits to follow local guidance and "remain alert to the changing situation".

According to Nepal police, 113 of the missing tourists are Nepalese, and 54 are from the US.

Excursion company Alpine Eco Trek, which offers guided expeditions and tours in Nepal, told the Press Association (PA) that 12 British nationals on its tour in the region - as well as two Irish nationals - were on an excursion across the Nepal-Tibet border and are believed to be missing.

Manager Kumar Adhikari said there was "not much info to share at the moment, but yes we have 12 British citizens (supposed) to make entry this morning".

According to the company's travel logs, shared with PA, the age of the missing British citizens ranges from 13 to 65.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said he is "deeply concerned" by news of the flash flooding, and wrote on social media: "All my thoughts are with those affected and with British nationals in the area and their relatives here at home".

In a joint statement with Australia, the EU, Finland, France, Norway and Switzerland, the UK embassy in Nepal urged British nationals in Nepal to "exercise caution in affected areas".

The flood hit early on Wednesday in Rasuwa, just north of Nepal's capital Kathmandu, with preliminary information suggesting it was caused by an earthquake triggering an avalanche with melted snow pouring into the Bhote Koshi river.

Dramatic CCTV footage showed a wall of water and mud hitting buildings near a border crossing and video filmed from inside a bus in Trishuli captured dozens of people trying to flee a flood surge that was surging through the valley.

Meanwhile Chinese state media outlet CCTV said a mudslide in Tibet's Gyirong killed three people and left 265 missing, with rescue efforts under way.

News.title: King and Queen to visit the Caribbean in autumn tour
News.content:
King Charles III and Queen Camilla will travel to the Caribbean later this year, Buckingham Palace has announced.

The royal pair will travel to Antigua and Barbuda for the Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting, with the King also visiting the Bahamas and Guyana as part of the eight-day trip.

The tour - planned for 27 October to 4 November - will "celebrate the communities, cultures and nature within the Commonwealth family," the palace said on Wednesday.

It marks the first time the King has visited the Caribbean since 2021, when he travelled to Barbados to see the country officially removed Queen Elizabeth II as its head of state and become the world's newest republic.

The monarch, who was the Prince of Wales at the time, acknowledged the "appalling atrocity of slavery" the Caribbean island suffered during a speech he made.

He also visited Antigua and Barbuda in 2017 following the widespread devastation caused by Hurricanes Irma and Maria, and made official visits to Guyana in 2000 and the Bahamas in 1973.

He travelled across the Atlantic Ocean earlier this year when he visited Bermuda in May, where he is also head of state.

The trip marked his first royal visit as monarch to a British overseas territory and came after a state visit to the US.

News.title: Yellow warnings remain in force as rain and thunderstorms hit parts of UK
News.content:
Downpours and thunderstorms will continue to bring the risk of flooding to parts of the UK on Wednesday.

A Met Office yellow warning for thunderstorms is valid until 22:00 BST, and was amended on Wednesday morning to cover northern and eastern Wales, as well as north-west England, the Midlands and parts of eastern and southern England.

The rain could be heavy enough to bring flash flooding and travel disruption, with lightning and large hail posing additional hazards.

Another Met Office yellow warning is in place for Thursday, when more thunderstorms are expected.

For some areas that have seen barely any rain so far this August, the next few days could bring the wettest weather in many weeks.

News.title: Boy, 15, arrested over stabbing at Brent Council HQ
News.content:
On Wednesday, one man who works in the area told BBC London the stabbing "felt normal".

"These things happen every single day here, in London and in the area. It's not a big surprise," he said.

"You see things like this happen all the time. You read the news and every single day there's something going on. If it's in Harrow, or Wembley, or Neasden, or Willesden or wherever, it doesn't come as a surprise."

However, one woman who lives in the area said the stabbing "came as a shock".

"I've never felt unsafe around here and it's a bit concerning," she said.

Student Demi said he felt "uneasy" after the stabbing.

"It's not really an unsafe area," he said. "It's a bit out of the ordinary.

"These things happen, unfortunately, but it's a bit strange to have it happen here."

Kate, another local resident, said: "Usually we feel very safe. We're fortunate living in this area because there are lots of security patrols and there are always people around.

"Stabbings are terrible tragedies, but it could happen anywhere, and I know there are areas of London that have to deal with that every day.

"I still feel safe. We're fortunate to live here with so much security; I wish that everyone lived in such an area."

News.title: Call with couple in Iran prison 'enormous relief'
News.content:
The family of an East Sussex couple detained in Iran say they have spoken to them for the first time in three months.

Lindsay and Craig Foreman were sentenced to 10 years in jail over espionage charges, which they both deny, and are being held in Evin prison.

Lindsay's son, Joe Bennett, said hearing his mum's voice was "an enormous relief" and encouraged the government to visit the couple as the UK embassy in Iran reopened last week after closing due to ongoing security concerns in the region.

A Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) spokesperson confirmed staff had returned to the embassy and said the pair's health and welfare was a "top priority".

Bennett, who lives in Folkestone, said the 12-minute phone call was their first official conversation since the couple ended their hunger strikes.

He said his mother told him she and her husband were "slowly rebuilding their strength" after losing a substantial amount of weight.

"Just hearing mum's voice properly again was an enormous relief," he added.

"We only had 12 minutes, but after everything that has happened, those 12 minutes meant a great deal."

Bennett said his mother and her partner had remained "mentally resilient" and "determined to return home".

Bennett claimed the conversation was "monitored" and conducted with an interpreter present, limiting what could be discussed.

He is now calling for the UK Government to take "swift action" to arrange an urgent consular visit and ensure the couple receive appropriate medical care.

He also hopes to meet with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and for the government to use all available diplomatic and legal channels to secure their release.

He said the family was particularly concerned the couple did not receive a full medical assessment following their hunger strikes.

News.title: Reform proposes £30 tax rebate for HMRC phone delays
News.content:
People on hold to HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) for more than 30 minutes would get Â£30 off their tax bill under a Reform UK government, Robert Jenrick has announced.

Reform's economy spokesman said HMRC's treatment of taxpayers was "offensive to working people" and his party would tie the pay of senior HMRC officials to customer service targets.

To prevent abuse, the tax credit for phone delays would be limited to two occasions in a given tax year, Jenrick said.

HMRC said its customer service had "vastly" improved over the past two years, with average call waiting times now 11 minutes and more of its services being delivered online or through its app.

In January 2025, the Public Accounts committee accused HMRC of seeking to "degrade its telephone service to drive taxpayers to digital channels" in a highly critical report., external

The MPs' report said nearly 44,000 customers were cut off without warning after being on hold for more than an hour in 2024 and "HMRC's treatment of taxpayers has damaged trust in the tax system".

Jenrick highlighted the findings - which were rejected as "completely baseless" by the then boss of HMRC - at a media conference in central London.

"Frankly, it is offensive to working people and I have had enough," said the former Tory MP.

"So, we will give HMRC a big incentive to actually provide proper customer service.

"I'm announcing today that under a Reform government, if you spend more than half an hour waiting for HMRC to answer your call, you will get a Â£30 credit off your tax bill. If HMRC delay, they can repay.

"And to make sure that the staff actually hit their targets, we'll tie the pay of senior HMRC officials to their customer service performance."

The HMRC said 80% of customer interactions now took place digitally, reducing the time spent on the phone to advisers, who were there to deal with vulnerable or digitally excluded customers or those with particularly complex problems.

A spokesperson said: "Our customer service performance has improved significantly with average call wait times now around 11 minutes.

"Overall customer satisfaction is at around 80% with more people than ever using our digital services, including millions using the HMRC app."

Jenrick also pledged to scrap UK privacy rules in favour of a "light-touch" approach to data protection as part of a bid to slash "red tape" for businesses if Reform wins power.

He said the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which mirrors EU legislation and was adopted as domestic law after Brexit, had "strangled" tech firms and small enterprises.

The framework would be replaced by rules modelled on New Zealand's privacy legislation, which Reform says has the lightest-touch regime still recognised as being "adequate" by the EU.

Labour accused Reform of wanting to "scrap vital safeguards that protect people's private data" with its "unworkable and unserious plans".

News.title: Household energy bills to hit three-year high as Ofgem announces 4% rise from October
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham acknowledged people would find the increase "difficult" but highlighted his move to cut VAT from electricity bills, which he said would help from October.

He said the government would "continue to look... at how we get energy prices down in the long term".

As well as the VAT cut, the government said the warm homes discount would take Â£150 off bills for six million households this winter.

But analysts at the energy consultancy Cornwall Insight have forecast domestic energy prices may rise a further 9% in the new year, bringing renewed concern to households during the coldest months.

Shadow energy secretary Claire Coutinho said the government must "put cheap energy first", saying while it had promised to cut bills by Â£300 they had "gone up by nearly Â£400 instead".

Liberal Democrat spokesperson for energy and net zero Pippa Heylings said Burnham needed to "wake up to the scale of the challenge" and make bold changes to lower bills.

Reform UK treasury spokesperson Robert Jenrick said households faced a "difficult period ahead" and said Labour's "net zero ideology" is driving up bills.

Former Prime Minister Gordon Brown also weighed in, saying the government should introduce a "machine gaming tax" and use proceeds to help those struggling with bills.

Longer term, he said Burnham should look at a social tariff for energy.

"I think Andy Burnham, I know him well, will want to do something along the lines I'm suggesting," he said.

Neil Kenward, Ofgem's director general for markets, said while gas bills were rising by 8%, electricity bills were actually falling slightly due to the government's VAT cut.

He said the gap between gas and electricity bills meant it would be cheaper for households to transition to heat pumps.

News.title: Nicotine vapes best chance to quit smoking, major review finds
News.content:
Smokers who want to quit have the best chance of doing so if they use nicotine e-cigarettes, a review has found.

The Cochrane team looked at 80 major trials involving nearly 30,000 people and found that nicotine vapes were more effective than traditional aids such as patches, gum and support plans - increasing the success rate by about 60%, from around six in every 100 managing to quit smoking to one in every 10.

They outperformed non-nicotine vapes too, although researchers say switching to these afterwards might help with weaning off nicotine.

And they could prove more effective than the new anti-smoking pill cytisine, external, which the NHS has started to roll out - although more research is needed.

News.title: Child among two dead in house fire near Middlesbrough as pair arrested on suspicion of murder
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A child is one of two people who died in a house fire less than a mile from the site of a crash on the A66 which killed seven people, police have said.

Cleveland Police said two men, aged 23 and 31, have been arrested on suspicion of murder and they remain in police custody following the blaze at an end-of-terrace property in Birchington Avenue, Grangetown, near Middlesbrough.

In a statement, the force said officers were called to the property at 5:23am on Wednesday and confirmed two people had died, “including one child”.

It said they have yet to be formally identified.

The force said that a 48-year-old woman remains in a critical condition in the Royal Victoria Infirmary (RVI) in Newcastle.

Three other people suffered injuries which are believed to be non life-threatening.

The force would not rule out a link between the blaze and the crash which killed two police officers and five young men.

Redcar and Cleveland local policing commander, Superintendent Emily Harrison, said: “We continue to work to establish the circumstances of exactly what has happened, but we are keeping an open mind and cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime at this time.”

More to follow...

Miley Cyrus has shared an emotional tribute to her godmother, the music icon Dolly Parton, after her death aged 80.

Parton’s death was announced by her nephew, Bryan Seaver, in an Instagram video posted Tuesday afternoon. A representative said that the singer had dealt with a “brief battle with cancer.” Parton was widely regarded as the Queen of Country Music, known for her timeless hits including “9 to 5,” “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You.”

Miley said on Instagram Wednesday: “The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share. Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts.”

“What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis.”

The post continued: “I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things.”

open image in gallery Dolly Parton often took the stage with her goddaughter Miley Cyrus, and the pair are pictured here performing ‘Jolene’ at the 2019 Grammy Awards ( Getty )

The duo, who often took the stage together, are close family friends through Miley’s dad, Billy Ray Cyrus.

Parton and Billy bonded when he joined her 1992 tour as an opening act to promote his song “Achy Breaky Heart.” It was during that period that Billy asked the “9 to 5” singer if she would be godmother to his newborn baby girl, Miley.

“We just got to be good friends because he’s a Kentucky boy, I’m from Tennessee,” Parton had said previously about their relationship. “And he said … ‘We’re having a girl, and you’ve got to be her godmother!’ And I said: ‘Well, I’d be honored.’ So actually, Miley and I took over from there. We just stayed very, very close through the years.”

Dolly and Miley remained close as the latter graduated from Disney Channel star to becoming Grammy recording artist, and the two singers have collaborated on multiple occasions, including when Parton made a cameo on Hannah Montana as the character Aunt Dolly.

Parton continued to make guest appearances on the show throughout its four seasons, including an episode in season two titled “I Will Always Loathe You” — a nod to Parton's timeless song “I Will Always Love You.” In the episode, Miley dressed up like Parton, wearing a platinum blond mullet-style wig.

The pair performed a rendition of Parton’s “Jolene” together in 2012 at the 25th anniversary of Dollywood, and Miley would go on to call her godmother her role model.

In 2019, the duo sang “Jolene” together again onstage at the Grammy Awards, where they were joined by Kacey Musgraves and Katy Perry.

open image in gallery Miley Cyrus has paid tribute to the music icon Dolly Parton after her death aged 80 ( AFP via Getty Images )

They also reunited in the recording studio for a reimagined rendition of Cyrus’s 2013 song “Wrecking Ball” for Parton’s 2023 album Rockstar, where the lyric “I will always want you,” was changed to “I will always love you.”

Over the years, Miley had praised her “Aunt Dolly” for supporting her throughout her career. After they collaborated on the “Wrecking Ball” duet, Parton said on X that Miley was the “most gifted person I know” and that she was proud to be her godmother.

The pair performed together at various awards season shows and festive events, including co-hosting NBC’s New Year’s Eve special in 2022.

In a tribute of his own, Billy Ray said he loved Parton with his whole heart, and shared anecdotes from their 1992 tour.

“In 1992, I’ll never forget walking into her dressing room to apologize for all the tabloid stories which claimed I was having an affair with her,” he wrote, sharing a photo carousel of pictures of them together over the years. “In true Dolly fashion, she just looked at me, winked and said, ‘Honey, this trash sells records!’”

“I have so many moments and memories with Dolly, it’s hard to know where to start. Like every little boy, I grew up loving Dolly Parton. She was a part of our lives, on our TV’s, right in our living rooms,” he continued.

“Dolly recently sent me a beautiful message, telling me she loved me with her whole heart. I will always love her in the same way ….. with my whole heart … and I always will.”

open image in gallery ‘The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share,’ said Miley Cyrus in a tribute shared Wednesday ( PA )

Musicians including Musgraves, Mick Jagger and Kelly Clarkson have paid tribute to Parton following her death. President Donald Trump ordered American flags to be lowered at half mast to honor country music icon.

Seaver, who had served as Parton’s head of security for more than two decades, said it was “an honor mixed with absolute pride and great sadness” to be asked to represent his family in announcing her death.

“But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly. Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents and countless others who have watched her and longed for her to meet them in the heavens,” he said.

President Donald Trump is reportedly considering additional tariffs or other trade actions against Canada as the two countries exchange retaliatory measures over failed trade negotiations.

The president’s desired escalation could range from imposing higher tariffs, beyond the already 50 percent on hundreds of Canadian products, to other trade actions, a White House official told Bloomberg Tuesday.

The unnamed White House official did not expand on the potential new actions but said people could expect the administration to respond to Canada taxing approximately $20 billion in American products.

The Independent has asked the U.S. Office of the Trade Representative for comment.

Trump appeared to hint at further action against Canada in an interview with Glenn Beck Wednesday, saying, “it's time to teach Canada you can't do this anymore.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump is reportedly considering additional levies or trade actions against Canada, after trade negotiations between the two countries fell apart last week ( AFP/Getty )

“They don’t have anything that we have to have, okay, we can get by,” Trump said Wednesday morning. “I mean, there are a couple of things that would make it a little inconvenient, but we can get them elsewhere.”

The president did not specify what “things” he was referring to that could be difficult to obtain.

A trade conflict erupted between the U.S. and Canada last week, after negotiations between the once-friendly North American neighbors disintegrated at the 11th hour. The two countries were reportedly close to striking a trade deal to prevent Trump’s 50 percent tariffs from taking effect.

The president has long complained that Canada, one of the U.S.’s largest trading partners, unfairly restricts U.S. exports of dairy, alcohol and auto parts.

open image in gallery Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney essentially matched the US’s tariffs this week, standing up to President Donald Trump after months of back-and-forth over trade deals ( AFP/Getty )

But after tense negotiations, Prime Minister Mark Carney walked away from the negotiation table, accusing U.S. officials of offering a bad deal and trying to make “last-minute changes” that led him to “question the reliability of any deal.”

“You’re at war when you’re attacked, and we got attacked,” Carney said over the weekend.

Trump imposed the tariffs of up to 50 percent on $20 billion of Canadian imports, under a provision of the 1930 Tariff Act.

Canada responded by essentially matching the U.S’s tariffs, announcing new levies of up to 50 percent on hundreds of American exports set to take effect September 8.

But Canadian officials are also considering other actions against the U.S., should Trump continue to retaliate. Ontario Premier Doug Ford, one of the officials leading the Canadian charge against Trump, threatened to cut off U.S. access to electricity and minerals.

“We power 1.5 million homes and businesses,” Ford told the Associated Press Monday. “Everything’s on the table. I’ll do whatever it takes.”

Ford has previously threatened to revoke the U.S.’s access to electricity in trade negotiations with Trump.

This week, Trump also threatened to rename Lake Ontario to “Lake America.”

Tim Curry, the charismatic star of The Rocky Horror Picture Show, has reportedly died at the age of 80.

Curry was famed for his extensive work on stage and roles in films such as Clue, Annie, Spamalot and It.

His manager confirmed his death to The New York Times.

TMZ was first to report that the actor died late Tuesday at his Los Angeles home. A cause of death was not immediately given, though the actor had suffered from significant health problems since a major stroke in 2012 left him unable to walk.

Born Timothy James Curry in Cheshire, England, in 1946, Curry was the younger child of Patricia, a school secretary, and James, a Methodist chaplain for the Royal Navy. He had an older sister, Judith – a concert pianist, who died in 2001.

open image in gallery Richard O’Brien (left) wrote the role that would define Curry’s career in ‘The Rocky Horror Show’ ( Getty Images )

Curry grew up in Plymouth and attended boarding school. In 1958, when he was just 12 years old, his childhood was rocked by his father’s death from pneumonia.

Ten years later, it was watching Judi Dench onstage as Sally Bowles in Cabaret at London’s Palace Theatre that made him determined to be an actor.

Actor and director Patrick Barlow recalled his days sharing a house with Curry while studying at Birmingham University. “I remember being amazed by his extraordinary singing voice – it was just completely perfect, just something he was born with – it came ready made,” he told The Guardian.

Curry burst onto the West End scene after graduating, when he was cast in the original UK production of the hit hippie musical Hair. To land the role, he lied to producers about his experience and claimed to have an Equity card, allowing him to bypass union rules that would otherwise have prevented him from being cast.

Describing it as a “liberating” experience – one which involved stripping off on stage – Curry played the part of the free-spirited hippie, Woof. He became good friends with his co-star Richard O’Brien, who went on to write the role that would define Curry’s career: cross-dressing mad scientist Dr Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Show.

open image in gallery Nell Campbell (left), Tim Curry (centre) and Richard O’Brien (right) in ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show' ( Fox )

Rocky Horror, a camp, sexually subversive rock musical, opened in London in 1973, and Curry took on the role for two years, performing onstage in New York and at the Roxy in Los Angeles. In 1975, he reprised the role for the film adaptation, The Rocky Horror Picture Show.

Starring Susan Sarandon, Barry Bostwick, O’Brien and Meat Loaf, the film became a cult hit of the highest magnitude and is now considered a classic of musical cinema.

Part of the film’s success has been credited to its popularity at midnight screenings, with audiences often dressing in the distinctive BDSM-inspired costumes from the movie. It continues to run in limited release to this day, half a century later, making it the longest-running film release of all time.

Speaking to The Student Television of Imperial College in 1975, Curry was asked if he had any hesitation in accepting the role. “I was hesitant in that, if it worked, it might be a difficult image to shake off,” he replied.

When that fear proved, to some extent, justified, Curry spent decades refusing to discuss Rocky Horror in the few interviews he gave to the press. He never turned against the film, however, and in 2016 returned to the franchise, taking on the role of the Criminologist in a made-for-TV remake.

In 1978, Curry recorded his debut album, a rock record titled Read My Lips. The varied collection of covers featured a heavyweight roster of musicians underneath him, including Dick Wagner, Bob Babbitt and Nils Lofgren.

open image in gallery Curry recorded his first music album in 1978, titled ‘Read My Lips’ ( Getty Images )

Curry would go on to record two more studio albums (plus a host of soundtracks), and toured with a live band.

Following Rocky Horror, Curry became one of theatre’s most in-demand actors, appearing in plays such as Tom Stoppard’s Travesties and the original Broadway production of Mozart drama Amadeus in 1981. Curry was nominated for a Tony for his role as Mozart himself, though he lost – in an inversion of the play’s plotline – to co-star Sir Ian McKellen, who played the composer’s bitter musical rival Salieri.

Other stage roles followed – The Pirates of Penzance; The Rivals; My Favourite Year (which earned him a second Tony nomination) – as did a number of prominent roles in Hollywood films. With a distinctive smirk, Curry showed a particular aptitude for villains, playing “Rooster” Hannigan in the 1982 film adaptation of Annie, and the nefarious Long John Silver in Muppet Treasure Island.

open image in gallery ‘Muppet Treasure Island’ saw Curry act opposite a cast of puppets ( Getty Images )

He went on to appear in films including Home Alone 2: Lost in New York, submarine thriller The Hunt for Red October and Clue, the star-studded adaptation of the board game Cluedo. In 1990, he took on his best-known television role as the supernatural villain Pennywise the Clown in the TV adaptation of

While Curry kept his private life removed from the public eye throughout his life, he did cultivate a number of close friendships with well-known celebrities, including Freddie Mercury and Michael Palin, who described Curry as “rather quiet” at first, but later “garrulous and at times quite ebullient”.

“There’s a soft, very English quality about Tim which is quite at odds with the Rocky Horror side,” he claimed.

open image in gallery Curry’s role in ‘Monty Python’s Spamalot’ in 2004 to 2005 would earn him his third Tony nomination ( Getty Images )

Little was known of Curry’s personal affairs, but he was said to be a keen gardener and a devoted dog owner. He once designed Mercury’s garden, though later recalled with amusement that the plants had died off while the Queen frontman was away on tour, with Mercury unaware of even the most basic watering requirements.

Curry continued acting well into the 21st century, on screen and on the stage, including in the production of the Monty Python musical Spamalot in 2004. (This role would earn him his third Tony nod.)

In July 2012, Curry suffered a major stroke and required the use of a wheelchair.

After this, he pivoted predominantly to voice acting, a trade that he had long honed across TV, film and video games. Among his prolific voice acting CV were projects such as FernGully: The Last Rainforest, Star Wars: The Clone Wars, and Peter Pan & the Pirates, the latter of which won him an Emmy Award.

News.content:
