City are expected to make an offer for Fernández and any deal would leave Chelsea seeking a replacement before Tuesday night’s transfer deadline. Chelsea previously told City to pay £120m by 14 August or miss out, but the midfielder remains a priority target for City’s manager, Enzo Maresca, who he worked with at Chelsea. Alonso started Reece James and Roméo Lavia in central midfield at Fulham, introducing Fernández from the bench.

City continued their midfield rebuild on Wednesday by buying Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a €100m (£85.7m) deal and agreeing to sell Nico González to Newcastle for £52m.

Sports.title: Bristol City ready to ‘supercharge growth’ and prove women’s clubs can fly solo
Sports.content:
As radiant, August sunshine glistens around a peacefully silent Ashton Gate before Bristol City Women’s pre-season media day, Hannah Buckley takes a seat, pitch side, with a gleam in her eye, surveying the scene. The sight of a top-class venue makes her beam in a way that perhaps only somebody whose CV includes job titles such as regional facilities manager and head of infrastructure, safety and sustainability can. Nice stadiums, particular ones used by women’s sports teams, give her a kick.

But after more than 20 years in football, the past eight at the WSL, Buckley is working on building something rather different: a club capable of thriving independently from the auspices of a men’s club. She was appointed as the Women’s Super League 2 side’s chief executive in May, starting her role in June, at a fascinating time in the team’s history, after they were taken over by the investment group Mercury13 last year to break away from the Bristol Sport group that oversees Bristol City’s men’s team and the city’s rugby union and basketball sides.

That breakaway has ensured it has been a relentlessly busy summer and Buckley, in her first sit-down interview, explains some of their changes: “Our headcount in staff has doubled. We’re having to put in place all the back-house services, which historically would have been carried by Bristol Sport. We’ve made improvements at the training ground, we have upgraded our training pitch, and I think I’d describe it as: ‘We’re in the marginal gain phase,’ reviewing what we have to do [to] supercharge our growth and success.”

Buckley, a board member at Somerset County Cricket Club, remembers the anguish she felt when told girls could not play football at her school when she was 11. She revived her playing days at university but creating opportunities for young girls is partly why she says it was a “no-brainer to apply” for the CEO role at Bristol City. There is a vast catchment area for youngsters across the south-west and she says: “It’s a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. It’s a true ‘build’ project.”

View image in fullscreen Hannah Buckley, Bristol City Women’s chief executive, says: ‘We are technically nine months old as a business.’ Photograph: BCWFC

Mercury13, which has investment from familiar names such as the former Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata, owns three women’s clubs: FC Como Women in Italy, FC Badalona Women in Spain and Bristol City Women. Their standalone focus on women’s football, without ties to a men’s team, excites Buckley, who recently led the WSL’s design guidelines for building or upgrading venues specifically for women’s teams. She says: “Independent clubs don’t carry some of the risks that you potentially see where the men’s club may get relegated or [have a] change in ownership and so the independent nature of the club for me was a real opportunity.

“What’s really interesting for me with being part of a multi-club ownership group dedicated solely to women’s football is the opportunities for research, the opportunities for cross-collaboration with different sporting competitions, and actually demonstrating that you can make it work as a standalone women’s entity.”

The owners’ passion specifically for women’s football has also invigorated City’s head coach, Charlotte Healy, who took over in June 2025 after coaching at clubs including Manchester United, Manchester City, Liverpool, Chesterfield and Derby. Healy says: “This football club, I really feel like it cares about its women’s team.

“We had to evolve the workforce – when I came in, I think there was probably [only] seven or eight staff – but we’re already starting to see that the people we’ve brought in the building are good people and we’re really starting to see the benefit of their expertise.

“[For example] we’ve brought a performance wellbeing manager in, which I think was really important – helping the players, because being a professional footballer is not easy, to come in and play under pressure environments and have to win. We brought in a head of performance services in January, who [has] great WSL experience – because we can talk about ‘being WSL ready’, but if we’ve got staff who don’t know what WSL ready looks like, how are we going to get there?”

Buckley adds to that list of hires by saying: “We now have a commercial director and a head of finance, we now have a full-time marketing manager, a club secretary.” And then there have been the most important recruits: players.

They include the 20-year-old Australia defender Alexia Apostolakis, who signed from Melbourne City in July and says part of the reason she moved from the other side of the world was “how ambitious Charlotte and the staff were to get promoted”. Healy says of the summer recruitment: “We felt we needed more squad depth, and I think we’ve made some really good signings. We’ve again looked at younger players. Alexia is one of the best young players in Australia.”

View image in fullscreen The defender Alexia Apostolakis, a summer signing, is described as ‘one of the best young players in Australia’. Photograph: Ali Painter/WSL/Getty Images

The Finland forward Lotta Lindström, who signed from London City Lionesses, says Healy’s team having been the top scorers in WSL2 last term was part of the attraction. The 21-year-old has for two years running been in squads that have won the division, with London City in 2023-24, then on loan at Birmingham City last season, and she says: “I hope I can bring up that winning mentality and [help by] doing those little things right, those little things that actually make the difference between being good and being the best.”

Healy is not shy about stating their goal, as they try to improve on last season’s fourth place. Last term, the top two were promoted, with the third-place team going up after a playoff against the WSL’s bottom side. This time, there will be one automatic spot and the sides in second and third will battle for a place in a playoff against the second-bottom WSL side. Healy believes defensive improvements can help them take the next step: “We want this club to be in the WSL. We understand the challenges that come with that – every team wants to be in the WSL. We need to be a little bit more consistent. We scored the most goals in the league last year and finished fourth, so it is really clear that we needed to be better out of possession. Our biggest evolution needs to be without the ball and making sure that we concede fewer goals – if we can do that, we’ll be right up at the top.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Buckley, who was part of the Football Association facilities team that developed St George’s Park into the national football centre and therefore is perhaps accustomed to a patient approach, says rather more cautiously: “I would say it [WSL2] is the hardest league to get promoted from – you only have to slip up once or twice and the opportunity goes. You saw how tight the margins were last year.

“There are so many facets to success – building the right culture here, first and foremost, is the important thing, professionalising our environment and setting ourselves up for success. I’d hope that we achieve top three. I think that would be a fantastic outcome. But I also have to be really measured; we are technically nine months old as a business.”

She points to their opening fixtures – away to Sunderland, another side taken over by a multi-club women’s-focused ownership group, the Bay Collective, then at Ashton Gate against promotion-chasing Newcastle – as a good “barometer check”, before concluding: “Ask me again at Christmas!”

Robins tend to thrive at Christmas. Whatever their final position, this could be an intriguing case study to observe how well women’s teams can fly solo.

Sports.title: Forest in talks with Celta Vigo over Javi Rueda as Axel Disasi joins Palace on loan
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest are in talks over the €15m (£12.8m) signing of the Celta Vigo right-back Javi Rueda, which would probably be their final incoming of the window after Liam Delap from Chelsea.

Oliver Glasner has been seeking someone who can play right wing-back and the 24-year-old former Real Madrid academy player fits the desired profile.

The former Spain youth international joined Celta three years ago from Madrid, who will receive half the fee. He made his first-team breakthrough last season, playing 26 La Liga games and 11 in the Europa League, helping his side to reach the quarter-finals.

Forest confirmed on Wednesday that the wing-back Eric da Silva Moreira will spend the season on loan to the Dutch side Excelsior to aid his development.

Chelsea have agreed to sell Delap to Forest in a deal worth £50m and have loaned Axel Disasi to Crystal Palace for the season. Disasi has also been borrowed by Aston Villa and West Ham since he signed for Chelsea from Monaco.

The defender said: “I know that it’s very tough to play against Palace at Selhurst Park – so I’m looking forward to being on the other side now.”

Brentford have struck an agreement with West Ham to sign El Hadji Malick Diouf for £35m plus up to £5m in add-ons. The left-back has been keen to leave West Ham since their relegation.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 5: Charlton Athletic
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 14th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 3rd (WSL2)

Prospects

Just under 20 years since Charlton’s successful women’s team were disbanded after the men’s team’s relegation from the Premier League, they are finally back in the limelight and ready to make a name for themselves again.

Karen Hills’s side impressed for much of last season, going on a 27-game unbeaten streak and possessing the meanest defence in WSL 2. A mid-season blip harmed their race for the title, however, and they lost out to Birmingham City on the final day of the season, ultimately going through a playoff to achieve their goal of promotion. Beating Leicester in that game will have given Hills and her players confidence that they can compete. There will be no complacency, however, having seen how newly promoted sides have fared in recent history.

Six players have departed since last season, including the influential Katie Bradley But they have been replaced with a blend of knowhow and exciting young talent. The arrival of Ashleigh Neville and Emily van Egmond will bring experience to Hills’s dressing room. Leah Davidson’s and Grace Johnston’s arrivals from Australia are intriguing moves. Meanwhile, Sophie Whitehouse was the hero of the previous campaign and Charlton will be looking to the goalkeeper to again lead from the back. It is the attacking side of the game that perhaps causes the most concern. Charlton managed only 31 goals last season, the lowest of the WSL2’s top six.

Preparations got under way with a pre-season trip to Cádiz, a chance for a new-look side to come together. There is no doubt that the task to stay up is a challenging one, but a club that have defied the odds on more than one occasion will believe they can do it again.

Off-field picture

A record-breaking partnership has seen haircare brand Sofnfree become the women’s team’s official sleeve partner. The branding will feature on all playing and replica shirts this season, while content creation will be a focus as Charlton hope to access new and existing audiences. The club have also launched their first women’s-centric TikTok channel. The news, however, that ownership group Global Football Partners have put the club up for sale could cause a bit of instability in the short term.

The manager

Reaching the Women’s Super League was part of the five-year plan Hills had when she was appointed in 2021, bringing a club close to her heart back into the limelight. The 51-year-old represented Chartlon for six years as a player, winning the FA Cup in 2005. This is the second time in Hills’s coaching career she has guided a team to the top flight, having previously done so with Tottenham in 2019, and watching Charlton walk out at the Valley against Liverpool on 6 September will inevitably be an emotional moment for her.

View image in fullscreen Karen Hills has guided a club into the top flight for the second time after have done so with Spurs in 2019. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Alamy

Star signing

Only three months ago, Neville was lining up against Charlton in the promotion playoff. Now she is a fully fledged Addick, joining from Leicester on a two-year deal. The full-back brings with her a wealth of experience having made more than a century of appearances in the WSL. The majority of those were under Hills at Tottenham after arriving there from Coventry United. A tough-tackling, intuitive defender, Neville never shirks a challenge and has the ability to push forward. She will also be a strong leader in the dressing room.

Stat attack

Despite finishing third in WSL2, Charlton kept the joint-most clean sheets and conceded the fewest goals in the division. No club saved as high a percentage of their shots on target faced, with Whitehouse playing every minute. She saved four penalties in the playoff shootout, too.

Set for a breakthrough

Johnston was named Charlton’s first signing of the summer during a transfer window that has seen many A-League players depart for Europe. The versatile young full-back arrives at the Valley hoping to make her mark on English football after three seasons with Perth Glory. She impressed during her time with her home town club, played every minute of last season, winning the club’s 2026 best young player award. Johnston’s form led to her being called up to the Young Matildas in 2023, representing the under-20s and now the under-23s. She was an integral member of the squad that won the Asean Women’s Championship last year.

What they say …

“I know what Karen’s about and vice versa; she knows what I bring. I’m really looking forward to working with her again” – Ashleigh Neville

Where are they playing their home games?

Charlton will play their home games at the Valley for a third consecutive season. Season-ticket sales started almost immediately after their successful promotion push. Alcohol will also still be allowed in the stadium, with an alcohol-free section established. Other fan activations include giving supporters the opportunity to sponsor a player.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Jean-Philippe Mateta to Aston Villa?
Sports.content:
Liam Delap may not have broken any records during his time with Chelsea but he is setting one on his way out the door. The England youth international is thought to be breaking Nottingham Forest’s transfer fee record with Oliver Glasner bringing him in for an expected £50m. The fee comes despite a disappointing 2025-26 season with the 23-year-old striker scoring only one Premier League goal.

Injury problems with his shoulder and hamstring did not help but the lack of return means the Blues were open to selling the striker and Forest have taken the bait. If Delap does sell for £50m it also means Chelsea will make a £20m profit on the player after buying him from Ipswich for £30m in 2025.

Delap isn’t the last deal Forest want to get over the line before Monday’s deadline day either as they are interested in Corinthians and Brazil midfielder André.

One story that is gathering momentum like a ball in snow is Jean-Philippe Mateta moving to Aston Villa. The Villans have made Crystal Palace an offer for the France striker but it is a long way off what the London club would like.

A departure that could finance Mateta’s move could be that of Ollie Watkins, though it is one that has shocked Villa. It has been extensively reported the English international has interest from Saudi club Al-Hilal with his signature set to be worth about £59.8m. Villa are close to agreeing the move and it is understood Watkins would have an annual salary of £12m.

With deadline day approaching, last-minute signings will come out of the woodwork at every turn. Let’s rattle through some. Manchester United are interested in Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, Newcastle have submitted a bid for Lille winger Matias Fernandez-Pardo, West Ham defender El Hadji Malick Diouf may play in the Premier League again with Brentford close to a deal for the Senegalese player, newly promoted Hull have agreed a move to sign Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin in a deal worth £20m and Tottenham are pushing to sign Omar Marmoush from Manchester City.

If Spurs did get that move over the line for the Egypt forward then the club’s spend this summer would be close to £400m. It is no wonder fans looked lost for words at Tottenham’s 3-0 loss to Brentford last weekend.

We started with Chelsea so let’s end with the Blues. Enzo Fernández, who was met with a wall of boos when Chelsea played Fulham in their opening fixture, may not play in London for much longer. Manchester City will submit a bid for the Argentina midfielder before deadline day. If they do, it could be the biggest transfer of the summer so far with Chelsea reportedly wanting £120m for the 25-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

So Fernández may travel up the M1 and M6 but the boos are likely to follow him after he scored and showboated in England’s defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final.

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential: Latest on two stars up for sale, the academy kid who could crack first team, the REAL reason Joshua Abe has gone missing, a blow for Florian Wirtz and why Andoni Iraola will be unhappy about draw at Newcastle
Sports.content:
Liverpool Confidential: Latest on two stars up for sale, the academy kid who could crack first team, the REAL reason Joshua Abe has gone missing, a blow for Florian Wirtz and why Andoni Iraola will be unhappy about draw at Newcastle

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Liverpool are yet to receive any official approaches for attacking duo Harvey Elliott or Federico Chiesa – but Confidential understands the club are willing to listen to offers for the duo this week.

All attention is on which forwards will join the club, but Anfield transfer chiefs also have the futures of several current high-profile stars on their to-do list. And neither Chiesa nor Elliott were part of the squad for the Premier League opener at Newcastle.

With multiple clubs in England and on the continent scrambling to get players – and replacing ones that leave – there is expected to be activity and Liverpool have not ruled out clubs getting in touch regarding the pair. Sources in Italy have ruled out a number of top clubs in the hunt for Chiesa, a Euros winner. Atalanta, Como and Inter have previously shown interest, though.

As for Elliott, the midfielder had a horrible year. Player of the Tournament at the Under-21s Euros this time last year, he moved to Aston Villa in a loan deal with a £35million obligation to buy – which would become active when he played 10 or more games. The 23-year-old did not reach that figure and returned to Liverpool.

Both Chiesa and Elliott had a chance to shine in pre-season but failed to take it, for one reason or another – Elliott is clearly not match-fit, for example, and Chiesa has struggled with illness.

And then young Lewis Koumas and James McConnell got the nod ahead of them on the substitutes’ bench for the trip to Newcastle. Head coach Andoni Iraola has taken a shine to Koumas and McConnell in pre-season and, as it stands, they will stay at the club this term – though that could change based on incomings with both attracting loan interest.

Liverpool are struggling to generate interest in fringe players such as Federico Chiesa (left) and Harvey Elliott (right)

SO WHO IS GOING OUT ON LOAN?

The aforementioned Elliott and Chiesa could, of course, fall into this category. If Liverpool cannot get fees for them, they may well have to accept a loan.

Koumas and McConnell, likewise, are both in the ‘to be confirmed’ folder after strong pre-season performances. Luke Chambers, the defender who can play left back or centre back, is in the same camp.

Chambers, 22, who spent the second half of last season at Charlton, impressed in pre-season. It is understood there is interest in his signature but he will not leave for the sake of it. Given he can fill in across the back four, Iraola could also opt to keep him around.

Youngsters Kaide Gordon, Keyrol Figueroa and Wellity Lucky may leave for the season, too, after Calvin Ramsay joined St Mirren this week. Kieran Morrison made a mad dash to Yorkshire last week. After travelling to Sheffield on match-day and signing for Wednesday on loan, he made his debut for the Owls that very evening and came off the bench after 68 minutes. He then managed 81 minutes from the start in a 2-0 defeat to Wolves in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night.

Luke Chambers, the defender who can play left back or centre back, impressed in pre-season for Liverpool and may keep him around the first team rather than loan him out

WHAT ABOUT BEZOS' BILLIONS?

Liverpool fans’ group Spirit of Shankly were due to meet the independent regulator of English football on Wednesday afternoon, it is understood, with a view to discussing billionaire Jeff Bezos' stake in the club.

The new statutory body was set up last year to protect the heritage of our game and also to ensure financial sustainability. Given the recent minority investment of around 38 per cent by Amit Bhatia and a consortium involving the world’s third-richest man Bezos, fans are worried about what it might mean for the future of the club and ticket prices.

SOS were to hold a video call with representatives from the regulator and want to know what the investment – which has potential to lead to a full takeover – means for the club, who will run it and how. The fans’ group were also frustrated when they found out the stake was closer to 40 per cent than the original reported figure.

Bhatia is the vice-chairman and is set to be at Anfield on Saturday as Liverpool face Nottingham Forest.

KOP KIDS UPDATE

One of the biggest positives for the academy this season is that talented teenager Joshua Abe is still at the club.

This time last year, as has been well documented in this column, 16-year-old Abe had half of Europe chasing him with clubs such as Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Real Madrid believed to have made a pitch to sign the forward.

Abe went on the first-team pre-season tour and had some exciting moments in the win over Sunderland in Nashville – but has rarely been seen since America, with the seniors or academy. The reason for that, it is understood, is that Abe is injured and is currently wearing his arm in a sling.

Jayden Danns returned to Under-21 action last Friday after an injury nightmare of his own in an eventful game against Everton at Goodison Park that saw Mor Talla Ndiaye have to end the match as a goalkeeper!

Liverpool star Joshua Abe, it is understood, has an arm injury that has kept him out of action

Jayden Danns has had a torrid time with injuries after bursting onto the scene in cup cameos three years ago - he has three senior goals in ten appearances for the Reds

GALAXY STAR COULD BE INCOMING

The pursuit of a first-team winger goes on but it's a fluid situation that changes every two minutes. At the time of writing, Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh has been nudged down the list given the south-coast club’s refusal to budge on their asking price of £70m.

A Gambian could be signing for Liverpool, though. Apparently young midfielder Musa Jatta Bajaha has had a trial at the AXA Training Centre. He plays for Gambian team BST Galaxy.

It would be a similar recruitment, if it went through, to the one for young defender Ndiaye. He was previously at Senegalese club Amitie FC having been spotted at an African youth tournament.

Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh has been nudged down Liverpool's list given the south-coast club’s refusal to budge on their asking price

STAT OF THE WEEK

There are a lot of damning stats to come out of the draw at Newcastle, such as the fact that Liverpool have conceded from more Opta-defined fast breaks than any side since the start of last season (nine).

You could also have the numbers about clean sheets, or the lack thereof: in their last 18 games, they have managed just two shut-outs, one against Galatasaray in the Champions League last-16 and another against Fulham in the league. But the most notable might be that the Reds ranked 19th for distance covered on the opening weekend, running 107.2km (according to Opta).

Fulham were top with 121.1km, which proves running is not everything, though big winners Chelsea (120.1km) Arsenal (119.8km) and Hull City (118.5) were just behind. Given Iraola demands intensity and a physical unit, he will want to improve those numbers.

FROM BAD TO WIRTZ

Data shows that Florian Wirtz was the most criticised player of the opening Premier League weekend online.

British Gambler used a social listening tool known as Meltwater to study all X posts mentioning top-flight players this week. Wirtz had a 43.9 per cent hit rate of negative posts, just ahead of Alexander Isak with 41.1 per cent.

Arsenal’s Christos Tzolis was top with the most positive posts. Does this mean anything? No – but it is fair to say Wirtz and Isak have work to do on Saturday as the negative noise around them is rather loud after just one matchday.

Data shows that Florian Wirtz was the most criticised player of the opening Premier League weekend online

WILL MUNOZ GET THE NOD?

It’s a busy week ahead with not one, not two but three cup draws! Sort of. First up, this evening, we have what the EFL are calling a ‘pre draw’ to the Carabao Cup next round.

Liverpool and other teams qualified for European football will be in that to decide whether they are home and away. That’ll be at around 7.20pm. Then, at approximately 10.15pm or after the Preston-Everton fixture, the ‘main draw’ will happen. Still with us? On Thursday, the Reds will learn their Champions League opponents. Hopefully some fun trips ahead!

Iraola is also set to do his press conference on Thursday afternoon. He will be quizzed on Saturday’s game against Nottingham Forest who have won at Anfield in the last two years. Any changes to the XI? Personally, I’d bring in Victor Munoz for Rio Ngumoha and do something to sort out that stinking midfield, but what do I know…

Sports.title: KATIE McCABE interview: Why I made the move that rocked women's football, the social media backlash after joining Chelsea from Arsenal and why I can't wait to win trophies at Stamford Bridge
Sports.content:
Of all the transfers that rocked the women's football world this summer, none were quite as dramatic as that of Katie McCabe's. Even with two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas and former Lioness goalkeeper Mary Earps WSL bound, McCabe's move across the capital from Arsenal to Chelsea eclipsed them all.

McCabe had luckily anticipated the furore, making the prescient decision to take herself off social media while it was being announced. As a result, she managed to avoid the areas of the internet which made for grim viewing as incensed keyboard warriors reacted to the news, although she is, of course, keenly aware of it.

Now, just over a couple of months later, it is easy to understand why when McCabe takes a seat with Daily Mail Sport at Chelsea's Cobham training ground to talk about her decision to move from the club where she spent over a decade to their fiercest rivals, she is choosing her words carefully.

'Coming into the end of my Arsenal contract, there a lot was going on behind the scenes,' she says. 'It was important for me to connect with the people I trust and the people around me who care about me and know me – I was leaning on people for their support.

'And then having conversations with the Chelsea manager and understanding what she wanted and the clear ambitions from the club, it matched what I wanted perfectly. I'm just delighted to get going now.'

Arsenal's releasing of cult hero McCabe at the end of her contract this summer was a result of a longer-term strategy intended to freshen up the women's senior squad and bring the average age down. The 30-year-old has joined long-serving players such as Beth Mead, 31, and goalkeeper Manuela Zinsberger, 30, out of the door.

Even with two-time Ballon d'Or winner Putellas and former Lioness goalkeeper Earps WSL bound, McCabe's move across the capital from Arsenal to Chelsea eclipsed them all

Record eight-time WSL winners Chelsea managed to bat off competition from last season's champions Manchester City for the left back's signature this summer

The fact the club decided to offer McCabe a new contract in April, as per reports, suggests they realised they had made a mistake. But by then it was too late. The wheels were in motion, and record eight-time WSL winners Chelsea managed to bat off competition from last season's champions Manchester City for the left back's signature.

Yet the intricacies of a football transfer, where countless conversations are happening behind the scenes, are often lost on the masses ('You can't expect everyone to understand,' McCabe graciously says).

In this instance, the vitriol was uncomfortable. Among them, one person shared a picture on X of a cut-up McCabe jersey. Another, who labelled her a 'snake', wrote: 'This is probably the worst thing Katie McCabe could have done for not only her career but as a person. You not only are hated by the Chelsea fans, but now you lose the support from the Arsenal fans who saw you as a legend.'

McCabe clearly anticipated that the fans of the club she has been loyal to for over 10 years would be surprised, but it's posed to her whether she foresaw this level of backlash.

'I think growing up the last 10, 11 years as an Arsenal player, being on that journey with the fans from Boreham Wood to what we had created to the Emirates, winning trophies together, it was always going to be difficult for the Arsenal fans to see me move on, especially to a rival club,' she says.

'I understand the frustrations and that, but coming off social media was more so the timing of everything. It was the first day of international camp that it got announced, and my focus was being away with Ireland. I didn't want anything to interfere with that, any outside noise.'

Social media abuse in the women's game is rife, with female athletes facing 19 per cent more online harassment than their male counterparts. It is a problem and unfortunately doesn't appear to be going away any time soon.

'I think if you're talking strictly football opinions, I'm all for that,' McCabe says. 'If people or pages tend to get personal, then that's another story.

Arsenal's releasing of McCabe at the end of her contract was a result of a longer-term strategy intended to freshen up the women's senior squad and bring the average age down

McCabe was lucky to avoid a third career red card in April when she pulled her new team-mate Alyssa Thompson's hair in a Champions League meeting with her new side

'I keep it at a distance. For me, the most important thing is what my team-mates think, the manager, staff and the people I work with around me and, of course, my close circle of people away from football. That comes with experience.'

Experience is something McCabe has in abundance. She may be one of the most successful women's players of the modern era, with seven major trophies in her cabinet, yet to the Arsenal team and its fanbase she was so, so much more. 'We've got McCabe', they would sing every matchday, which she happily echoed back to them after ending their decade-long wait for a Women's Champions League title.

McCabe is the type of player that you would love to have on your team but hate to play against. She is often viewed as the equal of Roy Keane, a useful comparison given she also wears the Ireland armband. Unlike Keane, McCabe has a surprisingly low red card count, just two in her career.

She was lucky to avoid a third in April when she pulled her new team-mate Alyssa Thompson's hair in a Champions League meeting with her new side. The incident, which she claimed was a mistake, saw her new manager Sonia Bompastor receive her marching orders.

And while much has been made of those childhood allegiances with Chelsea, the reality of McCabe's switch is far less sentimental. Chelsea signed her because they believe she can help them return to the top of the WSL and has experience of winning the one title that eludes them, the illustrious Champions League.

For McCabe, Arsenal may have been wanting younger blood, but she still feels like there's plenty left in the tank and didn't want to drop a level from one of the best clubs in England.

'I'm in a good space in my career,' she says. 'I feel good, I feel fit, and I still feel like I've got a lot to give, and I think that was part of my thought process. Chelsea are a team that have fundamentally won for the last how many seasons. I want to be part of that. I want to bring trophies to Stamford Bridge, and I know there's a hungry dressing room full of players as well that want that too.'

A player who likes to lead by example, McCabe makes it clear that she has no intention of barging into the place and immediately asserting herself, despite her leadership experience.

A player who likes to lead by example, McCabe makes it clear that she has no intention of barging into the place and immediately asserting herself, despite her leadership experience

'It's a new dressing room. It's a new environment. It's a new game model, so for me, it's about coming in, getting my head down, getting to work and earning the respect of my team-mates first and foremost.

'I've been working really closely with the team over the last few weeks, and with Sonia and the technical staff as well, to understand how we play. Then I can step into my role, bring my experience where I can and help the players around me too.

'There's two ways of looking at it, but for me, since I've come in, I just want to get my head down, work hard and show the girls I'm ready to be here and compete.'

McCabe won't have long until Chelsea host her old side at Stamford Bridge – they are just the third fixture to follow Aston Villa for next weekend's WSL opener. We await the home end singing 'We've got McCabe' with glee.

Sports.title: After a boozy culture of haplessness, England may just have stumbled upon a winning formula with players who can be trusted to make the most of their talents, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
After a boozy culture of haplessness, England may just have stumbled upon a winning formula with players who can be trusted to make the most of their talents, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England have played so many ‘must-win’ Tests over the past two years that the phrase is in danger of losing its meaning. Yet victory over Pakistan at Lord’s this week would reacquaint them with a feeling that has indisputably gone out of fashion.

Not since late 2024 have England won a Test series, a barren patch verging on a drought that has included the botched 2–2 draw with India, the Ashes debacle and a home series against New Zealand that spiralled out of control amid another of the drinking fiascos that is in danger of defining this team.

It doesn’t matter that Pakistan – one of only two teams below England in the World Test Championship – will be less of a scalp than any of their recent opponents. The winning feeling simply has to be restored in plenty of time for next summer’s assault on the Ashes, and England are in no position to be picky.

A couple of weeks ago, the return to the captaincy of Joe Root seemed to sum up the lack of options in the post-Ben Stokes era. Vice-captain Harry Brook was considered damaged goods because of his own misadventure in Wellington, and there were no other candidates – an indictment of English cricket’s production line.

Right now, the idea that Stokes might make a comeback against Australia next summer seems more absurd than ever.

Joe Root and England managing director Rob Key are all smiles at Lord's on Wednesday

The build-up to the Test has been dominated by the arrest of England bowler Brydon Carse, who was later released

Root must know it too, despite the strength of the two men’s relationship. When he was asked on Tuesday what he made of the fact that Stokes was there in Derby so soon after he was there in Chelsea’s Rex Rooms, he dodged the question.

Yet it is clear that Stokes’s absence from the dressing-room reduces the chances of a younger, perhaps more impressionable, English cricketer – Gus Atkinson in Chelsea, Carse and Matthew Potts in Derby – staying out past bedtime. So much for his oft-repeated assertion that ‘nothing good ever happens after midnight’.

And that’s why Root’s challenge now goes beyond winning, while being unavoidably linked to it: he must instil a culture that regards late-night boozing as an activity best left to 20-somethings who are not paid hundreds of thousands of pounds to stay fit.

Because of their own haplessness, England have stumbled across a set-up that may be better equipped to make the most of their players’ talents than the previous regime. The chat has moved on from stale exhortations – ‘express yourself’, ‘be where your feet are’ – to reconnecting with a public who have grown sick of the mayhem.

2nd Test: Probable teams England: 1 Ben Duckett, 2 Emilio Gay, 3 Jordan Cox, 4 Joe Root (capt), 5 Harry Brook, 6 Dan Lawrence, 7 Jamie Smith (wkt), 8 Gus Atkinson, 9 Ollie Robinson, 10 Jofra Archer, 11 Josh Tongue. Pakistan: 1 Imam-ul-Haq, 2 Shan Masood, 3 Babar Azam (capt), 4 Abdullah Shafique, 5 Saud Shakeel, 6 Salman Agha, 7 Mohammad Rizwan (wkt), 8 Ali Usman, 9 Khurram Shahzad, 10 Ubaid Shah, 11 Mohammad Abbas. Umpires: Allahudien Palaker (SA), Paul Reiffel (Aus) TV umpire: Chris Gaffaney (NZ) Match referee: Ranjan Madugalle (SL) Pitch and weather: The Lord’s surface, under intense scrutiny, looked green the day before the game, while a mixed forecast may encourage the captain who wins the toss to bowl first.

As Josh Tongue, who was eventually exonerated after the Cricket Regulator investigated his role in the Wellington night out with Brook, put it: ‘We had a chat before training on Tuesday and Joe said out straight we want to be the best professionals and we want the next generation to be in the best place they can be.’

If one upshot of a messy few months is that the players are looking beyond their bubble and seeing their place in the wider scheme of things, that can only be a good thing. It’s not that we should expect them to be impeccable role models: that is asking too much. But some awareness of their impact on the outside world can do no harm.

Any more of this, and Stephen Fleming will inherit an oasis of calm when he takes over as head coach in time for the tour of South Africa.

It helps Root’s cause that England now have a fast-bowling quartet to rival anything they have put on the field since Jimmy Anderson and Stuart Broad were in their pomp.

Jofra Archer appears to have put his injury problems behind him, Ollie Robinson is averaging 10 in his comeback season, Atkinson has a ridiculous record at Lord’s, where his 26 Test wickets have cost nine each, and Tongue – like Robinson – took career-best match figures last week at Headingley.

Assuming England stick with the team who won in Leeds by an innings and 103, they will feature an unchanged side for the first time since the opening two Tests of last summer’s series against India – another example of the stability Root craves.

Harry Brook, in the nets at Lord's is part of a rare unchanged England Test side

Jamie Smith is set to bat at No 7 and will keep the gloves as he wins his 24th Test cap

It has arrived, admittedly, in a roundabout way. Six of the players who appeared in the first Test against India – Zak Crawley, Ollie Pope, Stokes, Chris Woakes, Carse and Shoaib Bashir – will not play at Lord’s. And three of the XI here – Tongue, Emilio Gay and Jordan Cox – are yet to taste victory in a Test series.

On paper, it hardly resembles a recipe for success. But Pakistan, even boosted by the return from a hand injury of their captain, Babar Azam, will need to improve hugely on their Headingley performance even to ensure a proper contest, and Root’s dressing-room dressing-down on Tuesday morning appears to have been met by a captive audience.

If the weather plays ball, along with the capricious Lord’s pitch, England can slowly begin changing the discourse – and no one will begrudge them a quiet beer.

Sports.title: 'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup
Sports.content:
'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

A statistic currently going around about Everton being the only club among the Football League's 92 not to have won a trophy, a title or promotion, or been relegated, since the turn of the century has contributed to a pessimism which made a gathering of the club’s faithful last Friday evening very welcome.

The occasion, at the Denbigh Castle pub, a legendary gathering place for Evertonians in central Liverpool, celebrated the former Everton captain Mike Lyons, whose life and career have been charted in a fine new book.

The aching sadness underlying an occasion in which Lyons' former team-mates took turns to relate stories of the indefatigable, generous and hugely talented team-mate they knew and loved, is that the man in question is struggling now and could not be there.

His daughter Francesca, who lives near Liverpool and calls him every day at the care home in Perth, Australia, where he is living with dementia, reminds him how cherished he is among fans. Lyons, 74, knew that the event was taking place and he knows about the book, The Man Who Bled Blue, a meticulously researched and beautifully written biography by the journalist and author Simon Hart. But his brain has frayed terribly. His family and friends have helped Hart piece together the life story.

He would certainly empathise with those 21st century fans who yearn for silverware – any silverware – and not least the League Cup, which sends the team to Preston, David Moyes’ old club, on Wednesday night. Everton were reigning English champions, four days away from contesting a European Cup quarter-final, when Lyons made his debut in March 1971.

Mick Lyons made 473 appearances for Everton in his 12 years on Merseyside, scoring 59 goals

‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses’

With Everton team-mates Martin Dobson (left) and Bob Latchford (right)

Yet his 11 years as an Everton player did not yield him a single honour. Liverpool won 15 in that time. By 1982, Lyons was on his way to Sheffield Wednesday, missing by a couple of years the start of the glorious era when Everton won the FA Cup and two titles.

Had Lyons been at Friday’s event, talk would inevitably have turned to the League Cup – and his huge role in Everton's marathon against Aston Villa in the 1977 final, won by Villa in a second replay at Old Trafford. It remains one of the greatest clashes in the tournament's history and was the closest Lyons ever came to silverware with Everton.

Evertonians still remember the intensity of his celebration when he scored an equaliser in front of the Stretford End in the second replay. ‘Michael was more animated there than at any other goal he scored,’ his brother, Joe, tells Hart in the book. (To his family, Lyons has always been ‘Michael.’) Fatefully, he was then asked to push up as a utility centre-forward as Everton chased a winner – it’s a strategy still known as ‘Doing a Mike Lyons’ among Evertonians – and a hole materialised at the back which Villa exploited to score a late winner. In the seclusion of the car on the way home, Lyons wept.

This story teaches us, among other things, that barren times can produce some of the greatest heroes, like Lyons, and that the League Cup can bring such indelible memories that Everton, who have not always fielded strong teams in recent times, should see it as an opportunity.

Hart relates how, despite the initial Wembley final not yielding a winner, the team still appeared on a planned open-bus tour of Liverpool for which vast crowds turned out. The first replay, a thrilling 1-1 draw in Sheffield rescued by a late Bob Latchford goal, would remain one of Lyons’ favourite nights of his career. He later described the noise made by Evertonians that night as ‘something I’ll always treasure. It embodied everything I’ve always felt for this club’.

The biography’s title, alongside an image of Lyons with a gashed face as he leaves the pitch after Everton’s 1980 FA Cup semi-final against West Ham – another one they lost – captures his contribution. His myriad cuts, blows and collisions form a backdrop to the book. ‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses.’

The book’s beauty also resides in its small details, capturing the boundless enthusiasm and often comic innocence which accompanied Lyons huge professionalism and work ethic.

He drove a club-issue Lada with his name emblazoned down the side. He eschewed the posh Liverpool hair salon which the players attended for their curly perms in favour of the work of team-mate Roger Kenyon’s wife Jackie, a hairdresser. Mrs Kenyon and Lyons’ wife Tricia were in such deep conversation in the Lyons’ kitchen that the perm solution was left in the Everton captain’s hair for too long. It was a catastrophe.

Shaking hands with Liverpool captain Emlyn Hughes ahead of the 1977 FA Cup semi-final at Maine Road

It is now 31 years since Everton last lifted a trophy, the 1995 FA Cup

The League Cup is the only major domestic trophy that Everton have never won, and it is time they rectified that point

You could have heard a pin drop in that Liverpool pub on Friday night when Francesca Lyons told the 100 or so people gathered that her father would have been humbled by all this attention. The consequences of his repeated heading of the ball are the same that so many old pros have had to face, full on, and Francesca has been an impressive advocate for football's need to do more for them.

There is a reason why the book’s subtitle is The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons. The Villa captain in the 1977 final was Chris Nicholl, who lived with the form of dementia caused by repeatedly heading footballs during his playing career, before he passed away in 2024.

But Friday evening was about the life-affirming qualities of a captain and player who, Francesca insisted, would not have had his life any other way. ‘He has always been so upbeat and fun,’ she said. ‘He would have probably laughed off all the attention because he’s always been so humble.’

Moyes, who also loves the bones of Everton, has a deep understanding of Lyons’ contribution. He and his long-time assistant Billy McKinlay paid him a visit during an Everton pre-season tour of Australia some time back. The League Cup remains a trophy Everton have never won. Lyons, who still watches the club’s games from Perth, would smile to see them finally lift the three-handled trophy next March, 50 years on from that legendary three-game marathon against Villa.

The Man Who Bled Blue: The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons by Simon Hart is published by Mount Vernon Publishing.

Sports.title: Sunderland submit loan offer for Grealish, Brentford get their £35m man from West Ham... and Villa expect Al Hilal to pay £50m asking price for Watkins: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Sunderland submit loan offer for Grealish, Brentford get their £35m man from West Ham... and Villa expect Al Hilal to pay £50m asking price for Watkins: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Sunderland submit loan for Grealish

Sunderland have submitted a bid to take Jack Grealish on loan from Manchester City. All options remain open to the 30-year-old, who has featured as a substitute in City's first two games of the season.

United's Overy joining Sydney

Manchester United youngster James Overy is joining Sydney FC.

The 18-year-old right-back was born in Perth and is an Australia international.

His United team-mate Louis Jackson is in talks to join St Mirren. The 20-year-old defender is due to have a medical tomorrow.

Both deals will include sell-on and buy-back clauses.

Schlotterbeck to be made a Saint

Southampton have agreed a £3.8million deal with Augsburg for defender Keven Schlotterbeck. The 29-year old centre-back is undergoing a medical this afternoon.

Keven Schlotterbeck is set for sign for Southampton

Louza's a winner for Panathinaikos

Panathinaikos have agreed a deal to sign Watford midfielder Imran Louza. The fee for the 27-year-old Morocco international is worth £6.8m. Louza has travelled to Athens ahead of joining the Greek club.

Derby set to welcome Meister

Derby County are closing on Pisa striker Henrik Meister. The initial deal is a loan with an option to buy for £7.2m but the overall cost will be £8.5m if Meister joins Derby permanently.

Kabore completes Wrexham medical

Manchester City right-back Issa Kabore has completed a medical ahead of his £2m move to Wrexham. The Burkina Faso international has agreed a three-year deal.

Wrexham are also adding Angers left-back Jacques Ekomie who has completed a medical ahead of his £8m move.

Martinez offered to Chelsea

Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as Aston Villa seek a new club for their wantaway goalkeeper.

After his move to Juventus collapsed earlier this month, Martinez is now one of three senior keepers in the squad following the arrival of Zion Suzuki at Villa Park.

For more on this story click HERE

Emiliano Martinez reached the World Cup final with Argentina in the summer

Liverpool check on Palace's Sarr

Liverpool have checked on a deal for Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr, though any move looks unlikely as it stands.

The Anfield club have been assessing different opportunities in the market as they look to add two attacking players before Tuesday. They have not made an offer for Sarr as it stands.

For more on this story click HERE

Sunderland in for Brazilian winger Igor

Sunderland are in talks with Marseille for Brazilian winger Igor Paixao.

Leeds have previously checked on 26-year-old Paixao. Sunderland are understood to have made an offer earlier this week and talks are continuing. Marseille need to raise funds and Sunderland's priority is to add a winger.

They have also been in talks with Sporting Lisbon over Mozambique winger Geny Catamo.

Bees agree Malick Diouf deal

Brentford have agreed a deal with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf worth £35m plus add-ons.

Daily Mail Sport reported Brentford's interest last month and the clubs have now come to an agreement.

The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season.

Brentford have agreed a deal for El Hadji Malick Diouf of West Ham

Disasi in at Palace

Crystal Palace have announced the arrival of Axel Disasi on a straight loan from Chelsea.

The 28-year-old centre-back replaces Maxence Lacroix, who went the other way in a £52million move earlier in the window.

Disasi provides experience in the centre of Palace’s back three, with the Frenchman expected to play in the middle of Chris Richards and Jaydee Canvot.

Palace remain in the market for another centre-back following Chadi Riad’s injury during last weekend’s 2-0 defeat to Everton.

BOBBY MANZI

Brighton's £3.5m Orozco deal

Brighton are working on a £3.5million deal to sign 18-year-old midfielder Matias Orozco from Colombian side Deportivo Cali.

Orozco, a defensive midfielder, has been watched by Liverpool and Manchester United among others.

He is due in the UK to complete formalities of the transfer and is expected be sent out on loan initially.

Man City complete ins and outs as they wait to go back in for Enzo

Manchester City's Omar Marmoush will sign a contract at Tottenham tomorrow after having his medical today, while Nico Gonzalez is finalising his move to Newcastle with the second part of his medical.

City are signing Palmeiras winger Allan Elias - who will fly in from Brazil to complete his move tomorrow - while a City bid is expected to go in for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez.

City have confirmed the £85.6m signing of 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille. The Morocco midfielder said: 'Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world.

'It’s a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

'I’ve watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football and they have shown they are winners – this club feels like it’s built to win. The squad is world class and Enzo (Maresca) is a top manager.'

Ayyoub Bouaddi has joined Manchester City in a £85.6m deal from Lille

Aston Villa expect Saudis to meet £50m Watkins asking price

Aston Villa expect Al Hilal to hit their valuation of £50million for Ollie Watkins if they complete a deal for the England forward.

Watkins is keen to move to the Saudi Pro League club, who are offering a salary far higher than his current wages at Villa.

Villa have so far stuck to their position on Watkins and there is growing optimism Al Hilal, who have already had four bids turned down, will eventually meet the asking price.

Villa are also pursuing the £65million signing of Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea, who would effectively replace Watkins.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Monaco join queue for Spurs star Matar Sarr

Monaco have joined the list of clubs showing interest in signing Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr.

Monaco are looking at the market for new midfielders in case they lose Lamine Camara who has attracted offers from Crystal Palace and interest from Chelsea.

All options open for Grealish as clock ticks down

Manchester City are leaving all options open to Jack Grealish as the window draws to a close.

The 30-year-old has returned to City's first-team fold, appearing as substitute in their first two games.

He was on loan at Everton last season and their chief executive Angus Kinnear says they have remained in contact.

City have not ruled out a permanent sale. Nor have they ruled out another loan or an option to stay, though that could be with potentially limited game time.

Coach Enzo Maresca has not ruled out a move either, saying after Sunday's win over Bournemouth: 'He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best. 'Then it is one more week to go and we will see what happens. Not only with Jack but also other players.'

Jack Grealish is now back at Manchester City but all options are open as the window closes

Liverpool look elsewhere with Minteh fee too high

Liverpool are exploring alternative wing options with Brighton's valuation of Yankuba Minteh considered too high.

As Daily Mail Sport reported at the weekend, Brighton have been looking for a figure closer to £80million for the 22-year-old Gambian who is out until October with injury.

Liverpool had initially hoped to strike a deal around £50m.

Meanwhile, Celta Vigo are understood to be interested in midfielder Stefan Bajcetic but Liverpool have yet to receive a formal approach.

The 21-year-old started out at Vigo.

Yankuba Minteh is valued at around £80million by Brighton

Forest in talks over Celta defender

Nottingham Forest have opened talks with Celta Vigo for right-back Javi Rueda.

Forest are discussing an £8m offer for the 25-year-old who joined Celta from Real Madrid in 2024.

Tottenham have asked about Forest full-back Neco Williams but he is expected to stay at the City Ground.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Forest are also in talks over a £13.6m move including add ons for Corinthians midfielder Andre.

The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but Corinthians are holding out for more.

Javi Rueda (left) in action in Celta Vigo's La Liga opener against Valencia at the weekend

Palacios set for £23.5m Ipswich deal

Ipswich are finalising a £23.5m deal for Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios. The 27-year-old has agreed a four-year contract. As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Ipswich want £9m for midfielder Anis Mehmeti, who has offers from Wrexham, Birmingham and Derby.

Ezequiel Palacios is set to became the latest signing in a busy summer at Portman Road

Osmajic leaves Preston

Preston striker Milutin Osmajic has signed for Genoa.

Deepdale boss Paul Heckingbottom confirmed the move was on the cards at the weekend and added to BBC Radio Lancashire: 'The business we've done so far has been really good in terms of players we've brought in to replace, players who have gone out, but we've lost a lot of players. We've still got a lot to replace and now Milly is another one we've got to replace.'

Milutin Osmajic is heading to Genoa after three years at Preston North End

Sports.title: 'Julian Alvarez isn't the victim, we are': Atletico Madrid explode and say there is ZERO PERCENT chance of £130m star joining Barcelona - leaving the door open to Arsenal
Sports.content:
'Julian Alvarez isn't the victim, we are': Atletico Madrid explode and say there is ZERO PERCENT chance of £130m star joining Barcelona - leaving the door open to Arsenal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Atletico Madrid have expressed their fury over the ongoing Julian Alvarez transfer saga.

The wantaway Argentine forward has been the subject of much speculation this summer, with Arsenal, Barcelona and Real Madrid all linked with a move.

Barcelona's interest is believed to be the strongest and Alvarez has outlined his desire to move to the Camp Nou.

The 26-year-old was subsequently booed before, during and after Atletico's 2-2 draw against Villarreal on Sunday, and he then missed training on Wednesday after claiming he was ill.

And, with just days left of the transfer window, Atletico outlined their stance and sent a brutal message to Barcelona.

'The player is being portrayed as a victim, but the only victim of the Julian case is us,' they told Spanish outlet Marca.

Atletico Madrid have expressed their fury over the ongoing Julian Alvarez transfer saga

Alvarez was jeered by Atletico's fans before, during and after their game against Villarreal

'They have harmed us economically and socially. There is a zero per cent chance of selling him to Barca.

'This situation is not about money, it's about dignity. There is a campaign with many lies and half-truths that has been created.

'The only one who pays for this is Atletico.'

Although reports have suggested Barcelona are Alvarez's preferred destination, Atletico's stance could open the door to a move to Arsenal, with the Argentine not ruling out that option after being left stunned by the reaction of his own fans on Sunday.

Atletico have remained steadfast in their position that he is not for sale throughout the summer, with CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin saying last month that the club would not entertain any offers for the striker, even in the region of £170million, although it is believed an offer of around €150m (£130m) from the Gunners could be accepted.

Alvarez has a £428m release clause and Atletico have already rejected a £129m bid from bitter rivals Real Madrid.

Marca adds that Atletico are frustrated with the situation after Alvarez rejected the offer of a bumper new deal in March, while he also refused to adhere to their deadline for a summer move of June 20.

The saga has continually grown since Alvarez's comments during the World Cup when he expressed his desire to leave the LaLiga outfit in order to 'fulfil my dream'.

'I try to be an honest person,' he said while representing his nation. 'I spoke with the people at Atletico Madrid, and I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer. I want to fulfil my dream.'

Atletico's stance could open the door to a move to Arsenal in the final days of the window

Speaking earlier on Wednesday, Barcelona president Joan Laporta added further fuel to the fire when he insisted the Catalan side were still desperate to bring in Alvarez after reports circulated about him joining Arsenal.

'This whole situation has created a lot of noise,' he said. 'This is not motivated by actions taken by Barca. It is motivated by the fact that Atletico told us they were not selling (Alvarez).

'However, it looks like, from what we hear now (Atletico reportedly being open to selling Alvarez to Arsenal), they are trying to reach agreements with other clubs.

'We approach them to see if they want to sell one of their players. When they tell us they don’t sell, we let it go. But in this case, there are special circumstances that have been made aware that Atletico de Madrid want to sell the player to other clubs.

'With this context, our interest and offer for the player remains up until the end of the window, in case Atletico de Madrid want to sell the player. We are very interested in buying Julian Alvarez.'

During Sunday's game, the encounter was simmering with tension before Alvarez came on as a second-half substitute as he was booed while warming up, jeered again when his name was announced among the substitutes and met with louder whistles when he came on in the 66th minute.

A section of the crowd also chanted: 'Let him leave once and for all, let him leave.'

As the full-time whistle came, the hostility grew even more as the 26-year-old headed straight to the changing room while his team-mates saluted the fans, drawing another heavy round of boos.

Discussing the situation in his post-match press conference, Atletico boss Diego Simeone revealed it was actually the club's decision for Alvarez to not acknowledge supporters.

'The club staff told me that the club decided Julian should not go over with his team-mates to greet the fans, and that it was not Julian's decision.

'The club made the decision to keep him away and have him head to the dressing room. No, I'm not in a position to give advice to the fans. I think I need to focus on my work, which is to give my best on the sporting side for the good of Atletico Madrid.

'The only thing I know is that if Atletico Madrid wants to win a title, we have to be united. We need forwards, and we need important forwards.

'For that, of course, we all have to work in that direction to give the team what it needs.'

Sports.title: Serena and Venus Williams to roll back the years and play together in women's doubles at US Open
Sports.content:
Serena and Venus Williams to roll back the years and play together in women's doubles at US Open

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Serena and Venus Williams will once again team up again at the US Open.

The sisters will play women's doubles at the tournament after receiving a wild card Wednesday into the event they won twice.

Serena returned to tennis this summer after a four-year absence, and the sisters were set to play at Wimbledon before Serena had to withdraw after injuring her knee in her singles loss. They played in the Cincinnati Open, losing in the first round.

The Williams sisters won the 1999 and 2009 US Open doubles titles and are 27-7 in their nine appearances.

They last played in 2022, losing their match in what was expected to be Serena's final match in Flushing Meadows.

Serena, 44, played with Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles Tuesday, winning one match before losing in the quarterfinals. Venus, 46, is entered in the women's singles event.

Serena and Venus Williams have got a wild card into the women's doubles at the US Open

Venus, 46, was controversially given one of eight singles wild cards for the tournament too

The Williams sisters teamed to win 14 Grand Slam doubles titles along with Olympic gold medals in 2000, 2008, 2012. They shared the No. 1 ranking in women's doubles for eight weeks.

The 46-year-old Venus was controversially given one of eight singles wild cards for the tournament in Flushing Meadows on Tuesday.

She will become the oldest entrant in singles at the tournament since Renee Richards played at 47 in 1981, according to the International Tennis Federation.

However, many tennis fans were left in uproar with many believing the wild card spot should have gone to a younger player over Venus.

One fan wrote on X: 'Another year of wasting wild cards...'

'Venus does not deserve WCs any more,' claimed another. 'So glad that Fedal understands how to retire gracefully.'

'I will get criticized for this but Venus doesn't deserve a wildcard. A young female player deserves the spot,' added a third.

'Complete waste and denying a up and coming player much needed experience,' echoed a fourth.

Another wrote: 'What a complete waste, she’s stealing someone else’s place.. she’s washed up and will get beat in two sets whoever she plays #embarrassing.'

Sports.title: Crystal Palace boss claims Jean-Philippe Mateta will STAY despite legal battle with the club... and denies reports Ismaila Sarr is refusing to train after approaches from Liverpool and Galatasaray
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace boss claims Jean-Philippe Mateta will STAY despite legal battle with the club... and denies reports Ismaila Sarr is refusing to train after approaches from Liverpool and Galatasaray

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage says he expects star striker Jean-Philippe Mateta to stay at the club after the transfer window closes - and maintains that Ismaila Sarr is not refusing to train.

Palace and Mateta have been embroiled in a legal dispute over the validity of the unilateral one-year extension in his contract, which Palace triggered last season.

The case was heard by a Premier League tribunal at the end of last season - Mateta’s camp later took it to FIFA, which ruled it was not within their jurisdiction.

Despite the lengthy proceedings, the matter was only played out in public for the first time on Saturday, but Sage has no concerns over Mateta’s commitment to Palace.

‘I speak with him every day and, in front of me, I have a guy that is funny, happy to be here,’ Sage said. ‘He gives his best in every session. I didn’t see a player who has a problem with the club or with us, that’s why he played the last game as a starter.

‘You imagine if we had a problem with him, he would not play as a starter. Now it is just a problem that will be resolved. It is maybe (the problem) with the man but not with the player, if you want.

Jean Philippe Mateta's move to AC Milan fell through in January

'I think he (Mateta) will stay and, like I told you, he has the behaviour of someone who is happy to be here, who wants to be here and prepared to be here all season. That’s why I understand your question, but I have no doubt about that. He prefers football to his contract. When you love to play, you play.

‘The guy is wonderful. The player only trained for two weeks so he’s not perfect. If he was perfect, he would play every game and score 10 goals but that’s not the case for anybody.’

Sarr, meanwhile, has been linked with a move to Galatasaray and has not trained since the Turkish club had a bid north of £30million turned down.

The Senegal international was not in the Palace squad to face Everton last weekend, with Sage citing a groin injury. Reports in Turkey suggested he was refusing to train.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Wednesday that Liverpool have joined the list of suitors for Sarr before next Tuesday’s transfer deadline but a move is unlikely as it stands.

Palace have made clear that the attacker, who has three years left on his contract, is not for sale - though Sarr’s camp are keen to move him. A fair valuation, though, is thought to be £60million.

Speaking on Wednesday, Palace boss Sage insisted that Sarr’s injury has nothing to do with the speculation surrounding his future. However, he remains unavailable for Friday’s match against Manchester City.

‘For the moment, yeah,’ Sage said when asked whether Sarr will remain at Palace. ‘Because when you have three years on the contract, it is not easy to leave.’

Senegal's Ismaila Sarr has been the subject of interest from Liverpool and Galatasaray

‘Ismaila Sarr is in individual training because he is really in pain with his groin. But we prepare him, he needs time. I thought it would be quicker, but I am not a doctor. That is why I wait for him and we prepare for him to come back with us. No chance (he plays against City).

‘I understand that for everybody to have this kind of contact is difficult, because you hesitate a lot. But for the moment, he is with us. He is under contract.

‘He is injured and maybe you can make a link between his injury and the situation. But for me, he is honest and I have no problem with that. I spoke with him this morning about that, yesterday about that, too. And we just want him on the pitch.

‘All the rest is for the other people. Football is like this now, we know when it is the transfer window that there is a lot of noise, a lot of stuff for the player. Maybe some of them are not really comfortable with this situation - and their agent, too, their family.

‘That’s why it is not really a good period when you are inside in a club, but you know when it is finished we will only be concerned with our performances. We just have to wait for that.

‘It’s always difficult for a player when your name is associated with a club like Liverpool. For the moment, the most important thing is to understand the player is not able to play and is in treatment, and what happens with his potential future is really far from me.’

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
