World.title: Up to 400 children without school places, says education minister
World.content:
Minister of Education Kristina Kallas (Eesti 200) believes between 300 and 400 children will be missing from the school system by mid-September as Estonia introduces compulsory education until the age of 18.

From this academic year, Estonia has raised the age of compulsory education to 18 years old, meaning all children must attend high school. However, discussions have arisen in recent weeks about the lack of school places.

When a student is marked missing from the school system, it means the state or local government cannot contact them and does not know where they are.

The minister told ETV's morning program "Terevisioon" on Tuesday that many students have not submitted high school applications. This is partly due to students returning to Ukraine for the summer, but some Estonian children have also disappeared from the system.

However, students who have submitted applications have also not received places.

Kallas said holding students back a year to repeat 9th grade is not an option in many cases, especially if they have not received sufficient support throughout their school years.

"These students need a different learning environment, teachers and approach, and preparatory studies are intended precisely for children who have such significant learning gaps or health problems that they need completely different support from what they have received at school so far," she explained.

Kallas also disagreed with teachers that preparatory studies will actually help solve the problem.

Critical situation in Tallinn

Kallas said that the situation is currently most critical in Tallinn. "A child with grades slightly below average can no longer get into any school," she said.

The number of children from outside the capital applying to study in Tallinn has also been higher than average. This has taken places away from local students, she said.

Kallas said that all Tallinn upper secondary schools are currently full, but admissions are still ongoing at almost all of them. This means that students are constantly moving from one school to another.

"Places are turned down again, places become available again. You have to constantly be on the lookout for where places become available," the minister explained. She said this is very stressful and the system should be reviewed.

Karl Erik Kirss, chairman of the board of the Estonian School Student Councils' Union, said it is important that students without a place get clarity on the situation and should be allocated a point of contact from the state or local government.

Kirss explained that many students, particularly non-Estonian-speaking students, are currently uncertain about how their studies will continue on September 1.

"On Tuesday, we instructed our state schools in Tallinn that if a student comes in who appears unlikely to cope even in vocational education because, for example, they do not speak Estonian at all, they should be officially registered as a candidate for preparatory studies," Kallas said.

She explained that this would allow the ministry to know how many additional preparatory study places the state needs to commission.

Vocational schools a viable alternative

Kallas said that new curricula have been launched in vocational education over the past two years.

Significantly more young people are entering vocational education this year than in previous years. "It has become significantly more attractive," she added.

The minister noted that over time, vocational education will become a fully viable alternative after basic school.

Kirss said that the new curricula in vocational education help change students' perception that vocational school is somehow a worse choice than upper secondary school.

"Of course, the current situation, where upper secondary school places are full and all students without a school place are being directed to vocational schools, probably reinforces the perception that vocational school is still a second choice," he added.

The minister said Tallinn College of Technology has more than 400 vacant study places. "If you are interested in the field of technology, then you should definitely contact that school in Tallinn," she added.

If it turns out that there is no suitable study path there after all, the information will be forwarded to the Education Ministry and the ministry can deal with the child individually. "If upper secondary school places are needed, then in Tallinn they are predominantly provided by the city, and in that case the Education Department should be contacted," Kallas said.

World.title: Painting conservator: Soviet‑era artists had to paint with whatever materials they could get
World.content:
Polina Richter, a painting conservator at Kumu art museum who is researching Soviet‑era oil‑painting materials for her master's thesis, says that the scarcity of supplies in that period forced artists to invent creative solutions.

Richter is studying in the master's program in heritage protection and conservation at the Estonian Academy of Arts and is currently writing her thesis. Her research focuses on the materials used in Soviet‑era oil paintings — specifically the peculiarities of material use at the time and how artists obtained what they needed.

Richter said artists working during the Soviet period mainly got their materials from the Artists' Union shop. Quantities were limited, and artists were often allocated a fixed amount of specific paints. "Many came up with quite interesting solutions because of the lack of materials," she said.

She has not heard of artists making their own pigments when supplies ran out. "But certainly someone may have gone that far," she added.

Dentist tools in the conservator's toolbox

Richter's work at Kumu centers on preparing paintings for exhibitions. Many works have already been conserved, but some were restored decades ago and need to be reassessed before being shown again.

"Unfortunately, time does its work, so they need a bit of touching up again for the exhibition," she said.

Richter compares painting conservation to treating a patient. First, the conservator must determine the artwork's history and current problems, then choose the appropriate methods to address them.

Kumu's painting department has four staff members. The museum also has departments for paper, sculpture and frames. Workload varies throughout the year — autumn and spring are busier because more exhibitions are prepared then.

Before an exhibition, conservators assess which works need preparation and whether there is enough time to restore them all. The job also involves working closely with curators, storage staff and other museum employees.

Removing old varnish not always a necessity

A conservator's toolbox includes chemicals, primers and paints. "One of the most interesting things conservators use are actually dentist tools — something you wouldn't expect, but they're great for picking and doing fine detail work," she said.

Every intervention must be carefully considered. For example, removing old varnish is a decision conservators discuss thoroughly.

"Varnish is generally part of the painting. Since varnish yellows over time and undergoes various changes, you have to look very carefully at whether it should be removed at all," Richter explained.

If the materials of a work are not well known, tests are done before starting. Samples may be examined under a microscope or sent to a lab if needed.

Unexpected situations can arise during conservation. "These are usually accidental and human. They don't happen often, but the team tries to find solutions. And since we're conservators, we have to fix them ourselves," she said.

World.title: Court rejects request by convicted traitor for early release
World.content:
Harju District Court ruled on Tuesday that it will not grant convicted traitor Deniss Metsavas's request for early release under electronic monitoring.

The Prosecutor's Office does not support Metsavas's conditional early release, and the prosecutor maintained that position during the hearing. Tallinn Prison likewise does not support allowing the inmate to continue serving his sentence under electronic monitoring supervised by a probation officer.

Metsavas's defense argued that through his conduct and efforts, he has shown that he has drawn the necessary conclusions from his crimes and that continued imprisonment is not strictly necessary to guide his behavior.

When deciding on conditional early release, the court considers the circumstances of the crime, the offender's personality and prior life, behavior during imprisonment — including participation in activities that reduce the risk of reoffending or willingness to participate in such activities during supervision — as well as living conditions and the potential consequences of early release.

The court reviewed the submitted materials, written opinions from the prosecutor and defense, and heard the prosecutor, the convict and his attorney. Based on this, the court concluded that early release would be premature and unjustified.

The court agreed with the defense that Metsavas has several positive factors supporting early release: a stable place to live, supportive family members, vocational training completed during imprisonment, work in various positions such as librarian and instructor of math and yoga groups, no unpaid claims, and savings in his release fund.

However, the court noted that these positive factors alone do not guarantee lawful behavior after release. Metsavas also had a job, home, family and supportive relatives before imprisonment, yet still committed serious crimes.

The main substantive condition for early release is a reliable forecast that the inmate will behave lawfully in the future. Despite the positive aspects, the court considers the risk of reoffending to be high.

This assessment is supported by the seriousness of Metsavas's first‑degree crime, committed over a long period. In the court's view, the risk of new offenses has not been sufficiently reduced.

The ruling has not yet entered into force.

The court convicted Metsavas of treason in 2018 and sentenced him to 15 years in prison.

World.title: Systematic thefts jump 25% in first half of year
World.content:
Compared with other crimes, systematic thefts grew the fastest in the first half of this year, Justice Ministry says. They were registered a quarter more often than during the same period last year.

A systematic theft is a petty theft committed at least three times within a short period. Most of these are shoplifting cases.

Mari‑Liis Sööt from the Ministry of Justice said this rise in systematic thefts is not unique to Estonia. The same trend is troubling Europe more broadly, where shoplifting and organized retail theft have reached their highest levels in decades.

"If we look at Finland, the UK and several other countries, theft numbers have increased there as well," Sööt said.

Mari-Liis Sööt. Source: Ministry of Justice

As for why theft has increased, she said we can only speculate. One reason may be that the cost of living has risen.

"Criminal networks have also become more professional. Interpol and Europol say this," Sööt added.

Taivo Rosi from the Tartu Police Department said repeated petty thefts have kept police busy for years. It is difficult to claim they have suddenly surged.

"In grocery stores, people pay for part of their goods and leave some items unscanned. When such reports reach the police, it becomes clear fairly quickly that this is no longer a case of customer forgetfulness but intentional behavior — a kind of invoice optimization. They pay for the cheaper goods, leave the expensive ones unscanned at self‑checkout and walk out of the store with a straight back and a proud face," Rosi said.

Politsei. Autor/allikas: Martin Dremljuga/ERR

According to him, people still steal the same things as before: expensive food and alcohol from grocery stores, and costly construction and gardening tools from hardware stores.

"We can also mention the well‑known light vehicles and bicycles, which the police have been talking about for years," Rosi added.

Ministry of Justice statistics show that a total of 14,600 crimes were registered in the first half of the year — a six‑percent increase compared with last year.

World.title: Estonian defense company to invest €200 million in Latvian plant
World.content:
Wolfram Europa will invest €200 million to build an explosives and warhead manufacturing complex near Jēkabpils, Latvia, with production set to begin in 2027, the company announced Wednesday.

The 40-hectare facility will be built on land secured under a long-term agreement with Latvia's State Forests (LVM). Construction and production are planned in three phases beginning in 2027, with around 200 skilled jobs expected once the complex is fully operational.

Wolfram Europa said the plant will produce military explosives, warheads and counter-mobility systems. At full capacity, it is expected to produce up to 300 metric tons of RDX or 100 metric tons of HMX annually, as well as assemble 100,000 anti-tank mines and 200,000 warheads per year.

Latvian Economics Minister Viktors Valainis said the investment would strengthen the country's defense industry while creating high-value jobs and increasing industrial capacity.

Wolfram Europa CEO Magnus-Valdemar Saar said the Jēkabpils facility would be the company's first major production site as it seeks to expand explosives manufacturing capacity in Europe.

The company said in its press release that Europe is producing far from enough explosives and that it aims to fill that gap. Its goal is to become Europe's largest explosives manufacturer.

"Over the past 35 years, Europe has steadily scaled back its explosives and ammunition industry, which has also brought technological development in the sector to a standstill. Europe is rearming, but investment remains focused primarily on platforms and final assembly. This is the explosives gap: weapons production is being scaled up faster than the explosives and warheads that make those weapons effective," Saar said.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate against Iraqi dinar continues to fall
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar continued to decline on Wednesday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate dropped in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,539.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,545 Iraqi dinars and 1,535 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate declined, fluctuating between 1,539.5 and 1,539 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq’s financial revenues decline by 42% in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s federal budget revenues plummeted to roughly 35.94 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $27.45 billion) in June 2026, down from 62 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $47.3 billion) during the same month in 2025, marking a 42 percent decline.

According to budget figures, the income generated from oil exports in June 2026 reached 28.5 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $21.76 billion), compared to 57.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $43.57 billion) in June 2025, representing a decline of around 28.54 trillion Iraqi dinars ($21.79 billion).

The country’s non-oil income climbed to almost 7.44 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $5.68 billion) in June 2026, up from 4.95 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $3.78 billion) in June 2025.

Oil’s proportion of overall revenues decreased from 92 percent in June 2025 to 80 percent in June 2026, while the contribution of non-oil revenues to the country’s budget climbed from eight percent to 20 percent.

The World Bank’s ‘Global Economic Prospects’ report, published in June 2026, highlights Iraq as a developing economy that relies significantly on commodity earnings, especially oil.

The World Bank has cautioned about the effects of commodity price volatility on the financial and economic stability of energy-exporting countries.

Commodity prices have been vulnerable to periodic shocks since the start of the current decade, the most recent being the huge disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict, which resulted in dramatic swings in global markets for oil, metals, and agricultural supplies.

Iraq’s economic output grew by 0.5 percent in 2024; however, according to estimates, it contracted by 1.5 percent in 2025 before continuing its downward trajectory in 2026. It is expected to rebound to a 12.2 percent growth rate in 2028.

The World Bank mentioned that Iraq’s economy is one of the most vulnerable to regional developments, with its growth forecast lower compared to several other Middle Eastern oil-producing countries.

World.title: Iraq’s Gulf Keystone revenue unchanged as oil prices balance output decline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Gulf Keystone Petroleum, the operator of the Shaikan field, one of the largest developments in Iraqi Kurdistan, reported stable revenue during the first half of 2026.

The company’s revenues hit $82.8 million as higher oil prices balanced a 67 percent decline in output due to instability in the region.

The company’s shares rose by 9.6 percent following increased revenues and reduced operating costs.

The company’s revenues are nearly unchanged compared to $83.1 million in the first half of 2025.

Adjusted financial operating profitability increased by 26 percent to $51.7 million, driven by cost reduction and robust pricing.

The firm plans to increase output safely and begin a water handling project in the first quarter of 2027.

The Shaikan field is one of the largest oil fields discovered in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and serves as Gulf Keystone Petroleum’s principal asset.

The field covers around 280 square kilometers and is located about 60 kilometers northwest of Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan’s capital.

The oilfield has an estimated 416 million barrels of proven reserves. It has been in commercial production since 2013.

World.title: President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council visits Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, Faiq Zaidan, paid a high-profile, one-day official visit to Tehran on Tuesday to boost cross-border legal cooperation, develop bilateral judicial agreements, and address important security concerns.

Zaidan met with Iran’s senior executive, legislative, judicial, and security leaders, including the Iranian president, minister of justice, judiciary chief, speaker of the parliament, and secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.

The meetings focused on aligning judicial protocols and managing shared legal issues, strengthening legal relations, streamlining judicial procedures, activating cooperative security frameworks, reviewing legislative support for cross-border law enforcement, and addressing border stability and security measures.

Zaidan strongly opposed the foreign economic pressure against Iran, citing the latest US sanctions imposed under “Operation Economic Outcast.”

The Iraqi judicial chief indicated that Iraq will never forget Iran’s support during the US war against the country in 2003 and the war against ISIS terrorist groups.

Zaidan called for the full execution of existing bilateral legal and security agreements between Baghdad and Tehran.

The Iraqi official added that it is important to enhance intelligence cooperation, curb smuggling networks, streamline extradition protocols, and tackle the existence of anti-Iran groups along shared borders.

World.title: 30 Iraqi students join PetroChina Scholarship at China University of Petroleum
World.content:
Qingdao/ Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Thirty Iraqi university students are completing their preparatory semester at the China University of Petroleum (East China) in the coastal city of Qingdao, marking the inaugural cohort of the Pioneers of Excellence academic scholarship program.

The initiative represents the first time the Iraqi federal government has mobilized the state Training, Technology Transfer, and Scholarship Fund (TTSF) to sponsor undergraduate engineering scholars in China. Funded under the corporate social responsibility and capacity-building commitments of PetroChina Iraq – West Qurna 1, the program bridges bilateral energy development with engineering education.

The scholarship follows a customized “0.5 + 4” academic curriculum designed specifically by China University of Petroleum (East China):

Preparatory Foundation (6 Months): Intensive Mandarin Chinese language acquisition paired with foundation courses in advanced calculus, physics, and chemistry.

Undergraduate Degree (4 Years): Full Bachelor of Science degree tracks focusing on three core upstream disciplines: Petroleum Engineering: Reservoir management, well completion, and enhanced oil recovery (EOR). Mechanical Engineering: Industrial machinery design, refinery turbines, and pipeline hydraulics. Petroleum Geology: Geophysical seismic surveying, structural sedimentology, and basin modeling.



Selected through nationwide competitive examinations and panel interviews organized jointly by the Ministry of Oil and the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, the students represent diverse Iraqi governorates.

Bilateral Diplomatic Patronage: During the program’s official inauguration ceremony in April, the Consul General of China in Basra, Chen Peizhong, and the Scientific and Educational Counselor at the Iraqi Embassy in Beijing, Dr. Mohanad Najah Jawad Al-Shorofi, addressed the cohort, highlighting the importance of developing native technical talent to lead Iraq’s domestic energy sector.

Student Commitment: Class representative Mohammed Al-Tawous reaffirmed the students’ commitment to mastering advanced engineering curricula to support the modernization of Iraq’s oil and gas infrastructure upon graduation.

Industrial Synergy: Since assuming the role of lead contractor at the giant West Qurna 1 oil field in 2024, PetroChina has prioritized local workforce upskilling, transitioning bilateral energy ties from traditional equipment procurement to joint human capital development.

Hydrocarbons form the foundation of Iraq’s national economy. By equipping domestic engineering talent with advanced training at premier international energy institutions, the Ministry of Oil aims to build a modern technical workforce capable of operating complex extraction assets, deploying artificial lift technologies, and managing next-generation energy infrastructure across southern oil fields.

World.title: Iraq and South Korea finalize financing for air defense missile system
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Minister of Finance Falih Sari met on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, with the South Korean Ambassador to Iraq, Lee Jae-myung, to finalize the financing mechanisms for the contracted air defense missile system between Iraq and South Korea.

The high-level meeting was attended by the Chief of Staff of the Iraqi Army, General Staff Officer Abdul Amir Rashid Yarallah, alongside the South Korean military attaché in Baghdad, according to an official statement issued by the Ministry of Finance and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Key Financial & Operational Discussions

Contractual Financial Framework: The talks focused on operationalizing the payment schedules, legal frameworks, and treasury mechanisms required to fulfill bilateral contractual commitments without procedural delay.

Airspace Sovereignty Mandate: Minister Sari emphasized that securing Iraq’s airspace and modernizing territorial air defense capabilities remain national priorities to protect state sovereignty and critical infrastructure against external airborne threats.

High-Level Military Coordination: The presence of General Staff Officer Yarallah underscores operational synchronization between the Ministry of Defense’s procurement timetable and the Ministry of Finance’s budgetary disbursements.

Bilateral Commitment: Ambassador Lee Jae-myung and the South Korean defense attaché reaffirmed Seoul’s commitment to expediting technical execution and delivery timelines in line with agreed bilateral protocols.

The air defense procurement contract with South Korea represents a major technological leap for the Iraqi Air Defense Command.

By securing multi-tiered surface-to-air missile interception batteries, Baghdad aims to establish full sovereign control over its national airspace, replace legacy systems, and build an integrated radar and missile shield capable of intercepting advanced airborne threats, drones, and ballistic targets.

World.title: Chief Justice Zaidan and U.S. Envoy discuss post-coalition arms control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Dr. Faiq Zaidan, received the Chargé d’Affaires of the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Joshua Harris, on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, to discuss judicial mechanisms and the enforcement of the rule of law following the scheduled conclusion of the International Coalition’s military mission.

According to an official statement issued by the Supreme Judicial Council and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the discussions focused on legal procedures regarding entities and individuals bearing arms in violation of the Iraqi Constitution and applicable laws, as well as institutional frameworks to enforce the rule of law universally across the country.

Key Discussion Pillars

Post-Coalition Legal Framework:Reviewing judicial and legal preparations ahead of the formal conclusion of the Global Coalition against Daesh/ISIS mission in Iraq on September 30, 2026.

Prosecution of Unregulated Arms:Outlining judicial measures against groups and individuals possessing, displaying, or utilizing unauthorized weapons outside the direct chain of command of state constitutional institutions.

Universal Rule of Law:Establishing judicial coordination mechanisms to ensure that legal statutes and constitutional provisions apply equally to all entities without exception.

The meeting comes as Iraq prepares for the transition of the U.S.-led international military mission into bilateral security partnerships.Restricting weapons exclusively to state custody remains a core pillar of the Iraqi government’s institutional program.

By coordinating judicial procedures alongside executive security measures, the Supreme Judicial Council aims to reinforce national sovereignty, enhance judicial oversight over armed actors, and solidify internal stability as the international military mandate concludes.

World.title: Iraq’s GCCE and Germany’s Sutco sign major waste-to-resource deal in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The General Company for Carbon Economics (GCCE Iraq) has finalized a bilateral Master Agreement with German waste treatment plant manufacturer Sutco® to construct a modern, integrated waste management and resource recovery facility in Baghdad.

The agreement, announced by GCCE Chairman Hayder Al Darraji, was signed under the joint patronage of the governments of the Republic of Iraq and the Federal Republic of Germany, marking a decisive shift toward circular economy infrastructure and sovereign carbon market integration.

The facility is engineered to process municipal solid waste at utility scale, converting daily refuse into certified agricultural inputs, renewable aviation fuel, and internationally tradeable environmental assets:

Daily Waste Intake: Processing capacity of approximately 6,000 tonnes of municipal waste per day.

Organic Fertilizer Yield: Annual output of 500,000 tonnes of high-grade organic fertilizer, produced in full compliance with German industrial quality standards to support domestic agricultural self-reliance.

Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF): Daily production of approximately 100 tonnes of SAF, providing low-carbon aviation fuel options and diversifying downstream energy products.

Industrial Recyclable Sorting: Comprehensive material recovery lines to extract plastics, metals, and inert recyclables for domestic industrial feedstocks.

Carbon Credit Generation:Estimated generation of up to 2 million tonnes of certified carbon offsets annually, positioning Iraq to enter international voluntary and compliance carbon credit markets under verified emissions reduction frameworks.

Cross-Sector Impact and Macroeconomic Value

Sector Core Contribution & Operational Outcome Environmental Protection Diverts 6,000 tonnes/day from open landfills, curbing methane emissions and groundwater contamination. Food & Agriculture Security Delivers 500,000 tonnes/year of organic fertilizer, reducing chemical fertilizer imports and restoring soil health. Clean Transportation Fuel Introduces domestic SAF production at 100 tonnes/day for cleaner aviation pathways. Climate Finance & Carbon Trade Unlocks 2M tonnes/year in carbon credits to mobilize sovereign climate capital under international standards. Industrial Circularity Reclaims secondary raw materials to feed local manufacturing and recycling clusters.

The partnership between GCCE and Sutco establishes a new benchmark for public-private environmental investment in Iraq.By coupling mechanical-biological waste treatment with advanced recycling, aviation bio-refining, and international carbon credit issuance, Baghdad is turning an acute municipal waste challenge into a high-yield green asset class.

World.title: Govt pushes to make SCADA systems in power sector Indian by 2030
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Govt wants to end imports of technology used to monitor and control Indiaâs power grid by 2030, reducing dependence on foreign companies for systems that are critical to keeping electricity flowing across the country.

A committee set up by Central Electricity Authority (CEA) to draw up a roadmap for this has found that local content in these Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems is below 20%. It has warned that dependence on proprietary foreign systems can pose risks if there are disruptions in global supply chains or access to technology, upgrades and technical support is restricted.

SCADA systems form the digital backbone of the country's load-dispatch network, linking power plants and substations with state, regional and national control centres.

They allow grid operators to see what is happening across the network in real time and control equipment remotely.

The committee found that software is the easier part of the transition: 36 of the 38 identified software modules can be developed domestically in the short term. But hardware, which accounts for about 75% of SCADA costs, will be a bigger challenge, with 16 of 25 key components expected to be ready for indigenous deployment within two years.

World.title: UP: CM Yogi launches 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra', women aged 60+ to get free bus travel
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister

on Wednesday launched the 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra' scheme and flagged off special buses to provide free travel facilities to women aged 60 years and above in the state.

Speaking at the launch event in Lucknow, CM Yogi said the scheme was aimed at making the journey of women more convenient and dignified and strengthening their self-reliance.

"The maternal power that has eased the path of family and society throughout her life--our resolve to make her journey smooth and dignified is being realised in the double-engine government," the Chief Minister said.

Under the scheme, women aged 60 years and above will be provided free bus travel facilities.

The Chief Minister also said that on Raksha Bandhan, mothers, sisters and daughters would be provided free bus travel along with one accompanying person.

"The honour of maternal power and their convenience is our priority," CM Yogi said.

The Chief Minister said the scheme has been named after Lokmata Ahilyabai Holkar, whom he described as an exemplary figure of women's self-reliance and good governance.

"At a time when the country was in the grip of the chaos caused by Mughal invaders, Lokmata Ahilyabai not only achieved the goals of good governance and preserved India's spiritual and cultural heritage but also set an exemplary standard for women's self-reliance," he said.





CM Yogi said Ahilyabai Holkar had undertaken the restoration of several temples across the country that had been demolished or damaged by foreign invaders.

"Whenever the topic of women's self-reliance arises, we all recall the name of Lokmata Ahilyabai with deep reverence and respect," he said.

World.title: Dasgaja from the sky: Why India and Nepal are deploying drones over no-man’s land
World.content:
India and Nepal are turning to drones to map a stretch of their border that, on paper, is supposed to remain empty.

The area is known as Dasgaja, the no-man's-land or buffer zone along the India-Nepal boundary.

But on the ground, parts of it have been cultivated, occupied or built upon. Rivers have changed course, while thousands of boundary pillars have gone missing or been damaged.

Now, the two countries want to map that mismatch from the air.

At the 13th meeting of the Survey Officials' Committee in Lucknow this month, India and Nepal agreed to use unmanned aerial vehicles to map cross-border occupation, including encroachments in Dasgaja.

The joint survey is expected to begin after the monsoon, around September or October, and be completed within three years.

The two sides will then jointly analyse the aerial imagery to establish how much land is being used by citizens on the other side of the recognised boundary.

The move follows remarks by Nepal prime minister Balendra Shah in Parliament in May that India had encroached on Nepali land and that Nepal, too, had occupied Indian land in some places.





Nepal's foreign ministry later clarified that Shah was referring to cross-border occupation and encroachment in Dasgaja, rather than making a new territorial claim against India.

What is Dasgaja?

Dasgaja literally means "ten yards". It refers to the no-man's-land or buffer zone along the India-Nepal boundary.

There is some variation in how its width is described. Indian reports generally refer to a 10-yard no-man's-land, while a study by Nepal's Institute of Foreign Affairs describes a 20-yard-wide buffer, with 10 yards extending from the boundary on either side.

The principle is straightforward: the immediate area around the international boundary should remain free of occupation, making the border easier to identify, inspect and maintain.

Why India and Nepal are turning to drones to map a border where markers, rivers and land use have complicated boundary management.

In practice, that is difficult along an open border stretching about 1,880 km. The boundary runs through farmland, settlements, forests, roads and river systems, while communities on both sides maintain deep social and economic links.

Nepal's Institute of Foreign Affairs has documented people living in makeshift houses and tents within Dasgaja. Even when security forces remove such settlements, people can return.

So, while Dasgaja is meant to function as a buffer on paper, parts of it have gradually become intertwined with everyday life and livelihoods along the border.

An open but defined border

India and Nepal share an open border. There is no continuous fence separating the two countries, and people routinely cross it for work, trade, family and other activities.

An open border, however, does not mean an undefined border.

The international boundary is established through boundary pillars, maps and geographic coordinates. Dasgaja provides an additional buffer around that line.

Maintaining the physical markers has become a persistent challenge.

According to Nepal's Department of Survey, 8,554 boundary pillars were installed along the border. Of these, 1,325 are missing and 1,956 are partially or completely damaged.

A missing pillar does not automatically alter the international boundary. Its location can be reconstructed using survey records, coordinates and maps. But on the ground, the absence of a marker can make it far harder to establish where the boundary runs, particularly where fields, houses and roads are close to the line.

Cross-border occupation

The drone survey goes beyond Dasgaja. India and Nepal also want to map what officials describe as cross-border occupation.

These are instances in which citizens of one country live on, cultivate or otherwise use land that falls on the other side of the legally recognised boundary.

Nepal's foreign ministry said this was the issue Shah was referring to when he spoke about Nepal occupying Indian territory. It specifically linked the problem to the Fixed Boundary Principle used in riverine sections of the border.

What happens when a river moves but the border doesn't?

Several sections of the India-Nepal boundary run through or alongside rivers.

Rivers naturally shift course through erosion, sediment deposition and the formation of new channels.

That can create complicated situations when the legal boundary is tied to a position established in earlier surveys.

Under the Fixed Boundary Principle, the boundary can remain fixed even when the river around it changes course.

The result can be highly unusual: a farmer may continue cultivating land that a family has used for generations, only for a later survey to establish that the land now lies on the other side of the international boundary.

Missing boundary pillars and shifting river courses can make an already complex frontier harder to identify on the ground.

Nepal's foreign ministry identified such riverine changes as one reason for cross-border occupation. Nepal's Kantipur has reported that decades of river-course changes have shifted thousands of hectares of land from one side of the border to the other.

Most of the border is mapped

The new drone survey is not an attempt to redraw or rediscover the India-Nepal boundary.

Technical boundary work dates back to 1981, when the Joint Technical Level Nepal-India Boundary Committee was established.

After years of surveying, the committee prepared 182 strip maps covering about 98 per cent of the boundary. The maps were finalised in 2007 and excluded the unresolved areas of Kalapani and Susta.

India's ministry of external affairs has also recorded that the strip maps covering 98 per cent of the boundary were authenticated in 2007.

But the maps were never formally ratified by both countries as a final settlement.

Nepal maintained that outstanding disputes had to be resolved, while India sought their endorsement.

Even so, they remain an important technical reference.

Why are boundary pillars a problem?

A boundary line on a map can be difficult to identify in a field without a physical marker.

That is why India and Nepal maintain thousands of boundary pillars along the frontier. But many have been damaged, destroyed or lost, particularly in areas affected by rivers and erosion.

The two countries have been working to restore them. At the seventh meeting of the Boundary Working Group in July 2025, India and Nepal agreed to jointly construct new pillars and repair damaged ones as part of their technical boundary work.

Established in 2014, the Boundary Working Group deals with issues including the clearing of no-man's-land, construction and maintenance of boundary pillars, updating cross-border property records and other technical border matters.

It does not cover the unresolved Kalapani and Susta disputes.

The technical mechanism operates at three levels: the Boundary Working Group, the Survey Officials' Committee and Joint Field Survey Teams. Field teams conduct ground surveys, while the SOC and BWG examine the findings and determine the next technical steps.

India and Nepal are using drone technology to survey parts of their open border where physical markers and changing landscapes create uncertainty.

Why use drones now?

The immediate objective is simple: get a far more precise picture of what is happening on the ground.

The UAVs will capture aerial images of areas where cross-border occupation is suspected. Indian and Nepali officials will then analyse the imagery jointly and compare it with existing maps, coordinates, boundary pillars and field records.

Aerial imagery can show precisely where fields, houses, roads, rivers and other physical features sit in relation to the established boundary.

But the most important element is not the drone.

It is the joint verification.

If both countries work from the same imagery and agree on the technical facts of a particular location, it becomes easier to determine what needs to happen next.

The jointly verified record could eventually provide a basis for negotiating the removal of encroachments, restoration of land or, where necessary, compensation.

Is this related to Kalapani and Lipulekh?

The India-Nepal border has several separate disputes.

Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura concern Nepal's territorial claims in the western sector and competing interpretations of historical maps, documents and the course of the Kali or Mahakali River.

Susta is another separate dispute involving changes in the course of the Gandak or Narayani River.

The current technical mechanism does not cover these unresolved areas. The 2025 BWG agreement specifically kept Susta and Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura outside its technical work.

The Dasgaja exercise is narrower. It deals with no-man's-land, boundary infrastructure and cross-border occupation along the established boundary.

What this drone survey really means

At first glance, sending drones over Dasgaja may look like a relatively routine surveying exercise. It is anything but.

The India-Nepal border is unusual: open to people, but fixed in law; socially intertwined, but internationally sovereign. Over decades, rivers have shifted, settlements have expanded, farms have crossed invisible lines and boundary markers have disappeared.

That has created a gap between the border that exists on maps and the border experienced on the ground.

The drones are an attempt to close that gap with evidence.

They will not settle Kalapani. They will not redraw the map. And they will not, by themselves, resolve every dispute over land.

But they could give India and Nepal something that has often been missing in sensitive border discussions: a shared, current and verifiable picture of what is actually happening on the ground.

World.title: Nepal flash flood unlikely to pose major threat to UP; 105 Indians among missing tourists
World.content:
The impact of the increased flow was expected to reach the barrage after around 8 pm on Wednesday.

Advisory by Nepal tourism board

LUCKNOW: The flash flood in Nepal on Wednesday is unlikely to cause major flooding in Uttar Pradesh, with the Gandak expected to remain below the danger level as the increased flow passes along Maharajganj and Kushinagar before moving into Bihar, a senior irrigation department official said.Speaking to TOI, Vikash Kumar Singh, Chief Engineer-II (Gandak), irrigation department, said there was no immediate reason to panic, though the local district administration and irrigation authorities had been put on alert and officials were deployed at vulnerable sites.âLast year, we successfully passed a discharge of around six lakh cusecs. There is no need to panic this time,â Singh said.Singh said the surge would reach the Valmiki Barrage near the Nepal-Bihar border and subsequently pass along Maharajganj and Kushinagar before proceeding into Bihar. Deoria will not fall in the path of this floodwater, he clarified.According to Singh, a sharp rise was recorded in the Trishuli river, a tributary of the Gandak, on Wednesday morning. At one stage, the water level was rising at around 20 cm per minute. However, the river subsequently began falling rapidly.The impact of the increased flow was expected to reach the barrage after around 8 pm on Wednesday. Singh said mountain rivers have steep gradients, resulting in both rapid rises and falls.As a precaution, canals have temporarily been closed because flash floods from the hills carry large quantities of silt. They will be reopened once the high-silt flow passes.Singh said officials currently do not expect the Gandak to cross the danger level or spill into agricultural fields in Uttar Pradesh. The affected river stretch along UP is roughly 30 km before the flow continues into Bihar.âThere is no need to panic. Everyone is prepared, and all our officials are working on the ground,â Singh said.Meanwhile, at least 105 Indian nationals were among hundreds of tourists reported missing following the flash flood in Nepal.According to a preliminary situation update issued by the Nepal Tourism Board on Wednesday, 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, were reported missing from the affected areas. The board said the information was preliminary and was being verified and cross-checked with travel agencies, guides, local authorities and security agencies.The list includes 59 Indians travelling with Samrat Tours & Travels and another 46 Indians with Leaf Holiday, taking the number of Indians identified in the preliminary missing list to 105. The nationalities of several other foreign travellers were yet to be confirmed.The Nepal Tourism Board said the flash flood struck the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa at around 8.30 am on Wednesday.

Statement posted by the MEA in regards to the report

NEW DELHI: India has rejected concerns raised by a UN committee over alleged racial discrimination and rights violations by law enforcement agencies, calling references in the panel's report âpolitically motivatedâ and âhighly maliciousâ.The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the observations were made after the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) reviewed India's implementation of the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD) in Geneva on August 11-12.The ministry said India had participated in the review in a spirit of constructive engagement and remained firmly committed to combating racial discrimination.The MEA described the exercise as a routine treaty-body review in which India participated in the spirit of constructive engagement. It said India's commitment to combating racial discrimination remained unwavering, noting that India had played a leading role in negotiating and drafting the convention in the 1960s.It said the Indian delegation had highlighted the country's constitutional safeguards, legal framework, pluralistic character, affirmative action programmes, democratic accountability and judicial remedies.âWhile we will respond to the Committee's observations through the established procedure, the inter-Ministerial delegation, which was led by the Solicitor General of India, Shri Tushar Mehta, had already rejected the sweeping generalisations, unsubstantiated allegations, or tendency to exceed the Convention's mandate during the review meeting,â the MEA said.âIndia rejects any politically motivated highly malicious references in the report with all the contempt that it deserves,â it added.

World.title: Congress, CPI criticise AINRC-BJP government for presenting a ‘lacklustre’ Budget
World.content:
The Congress and the Communist Party of India have criticised the AINRC-BJP government for presenting a “lacklustre” budget.

In separate statements, both the parties have criticised Chief Minister N. Rangasamy for presenting the budget without any vision.

Member of Parliament and chief of Puducherry Pradesh Congress Committee V. Vaithilingam said the 2026-27 budget presented by the Chief Minister in the Legislative Assembly on August 24 was very “disappointing.” There was no concrete plan in the budget to address the unemployment problem and infrastructure requirements of Puducherry.

Though the foundation for a grade separator was laid months ago, work was yet to commence. Also, the budget has not provided any clear timeline for the expansion of Puducherry Airport, the PPCC chief said.

He also criticised the AINRC-BJP government for its silence on conducting local body elections though Prime Minister Narendra Modi had made a promise to hold polls during his election campaign in 2021. “The NDA was in power from 2021 in Puducherry. However, the AINRC-BJP government has not taken any step to hold the elections,” the PPCC chief said.

Lacks initiative, says CPI

Secretary of CPI A. M. Saleem in his statement said the budget lacked initiative to address the needs of farmers, youth, socially-deprived sections and women. Villages in Karayamputhur, Embalem, Karikalampakkam and Panayadikuppam where members of Dalit communities were residing in large numbers lacked basic amenities, including proper roads, drinking water and drainage facilities.

Of the budgetary outlay of ₹14,300 crore presented by the Chief Minister, majority of the allocation was towards salary, pension and repayment of loans. There were no major schemes announced in the budget to address the issues faced by people, including growing traffic congestion in the town, he said.

The CPI also criticised the government for not making any mention of local body elections. The local body polls had not been held for a long time in Puducherry, he said.

World.title: Jairam Ramesh seeks Kargil-style review of Operation Sindoor after General Chauhan remarks
World.content:
A day after former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan made fresh remarks on Operation Sindoor, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) called for a comprehensive official review of the military operation on the lines of the Kargil Review Committee.

Mr. Ramesh, Congress general secretary (communications), said Gen. Chauhan’s latest remarks, coupled with his earlier revelations, had raised understandable concern and warranted a structured review of the operation.

Vital revelations

“In a media interview given in Singapore on May 30th, 2025, the-then Chief of Defence Staff Gen Anil Chauhan had made some very significant revelations on Operation Sindoor. Just yesterday Gen. Chauhan has again made some very important revelations that have raised understandable concern,” Mr. Ramesh said in a post on X.

He recalled that four days after the Kargil War ended, the then Atal Bihari Vajpayee government had, on July 29, 1999, constituted the Kargil Review Committee under the chairmanship of top security analyst K. Subrahmanyam.

The committee’s report was tabled in Parliament on February 23, 2000.

“Headline-grabbing revelations being made from time to time in interviews and lectures, whether part of a deliberate strategy or not, are no substitute for a structured and comprehensive review exercise like what the Subrahmanyam committee had carried out,” Mr. Ramesh said.

The demand came after Gen. Chauhan, speaking at the ‘VIMARSH’ event on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath at the Vivekananda International Foundation on Tuesday, said a loitering munition deployed during the operation may have struck the Kirana Hills area near Sargodha in Pakistan, where nuclear-related facilities are located.

The remarks appeared to differ from the position articulated during the operation. At a media briefing on May 12, then Director General of Air Operations Air Marshal A.K. Bharti had said that the Indian armed forces had not targeted the nuclear facility at Kirana Hills.

Gen. Chauhan also made a significant assertion on the ceasefire understanding between India and Pakistan, rejecting claims that U.S. President Donald Trump had mediated the cessation of hostilities.

“The ceasefire was decided between two DGMOs, and that’s it. I don’t see the role of anyone else,” the retired officer said. He also questioned how information about the impending ceasefire reached the U.S. side before India could announce it, saying he was certain that the information had not leaked from the Indian side.

Operation Sindoor was launched by India in response to the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack. Indian forces carried out strikes on terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir on May 7, followed by several days of military confrontation before the ceasefire understanding on May 10.

World.title: Interim V-C of MSU appointed
World.content:
Prof. S. Prabhakar of Department of English, Manonmaniam Sundaranar University has been appointed as the Interim Vice-Chancellor of the University as the one-year extension given to outgoing V-C N. Chandrasekar ended recently.

Dr. Prabhakar assumed office as Interim Vice-Chancellor on last Saturday (August 22), an official statement from MSU said on Wednesday.

He would take care of uninterrupted administrative and academic activities of MSU until the Syndicate Committee of the University meets again to decide on the future course, the statement said.

World.title: Nepal flash flood: What triggered the deadly Himalayan disaster?
World.content: A devastating flash flood has struck Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, leaving at least eight people dead and hundreds reported missing. The disaster swept through the Bhote Koshi River basin, causing widespread destruction to villages, roads, bridges and major hydropower projects. Authorities say hundreds of travellers are unaccounted for, including foreign tourists from several countries. Rescue teams, supported by helicopters and emergency personnel, are continuing search and evacuation operations across the affected region.

World.title: BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of hypocrisy over women’s empowerment
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) accused Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and the Congress of hypocrisy over women’s empowerment, citing what it described as inappropriate remarks by several Congress leaders.

At a press conference, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj accused Mr. Gandhi of “misogyny” and referred to a recent Congress event.

“Ten days ago, Mr. Gandhi himself participated with Sandeep Dikshit in a very cheap joke targeting a woman Prime Minister, and that too the Prime Minister of our friendly country, Italy, Ms. Meloni. It was almost like you were overhearing boys talking in a local room....,” she said, alleging that Mr. Gandhi’s “smash the patriarchy” remarks in Pune were an attempt to divert attention from the controversy.

“You want to smash the patriarchy? I am very comfortable singing Christmas carols on Christmas, singing Vande Mataram in its entirety, and reciting the Shiv Tandav. I challenge you: If you want to actually smash the patriarchy, then sing Vande Mataram in its entirety...,” Ms. Swaraj said.

She said that had Mr. Gandhi truly wanted to act on women’s empowerment, he would not have strongly opposed the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.

“Mr. Gandhi has neither a vision nor any positive agenda. That is why whatever his research team writes down on a piece of paper and gives him, he tries to use it to mislead the youth of this country,” Ms. Swaraj said, adding that the Congress leader’s “smash the patriarchy” slogan was hypocritical.

“Why the selective outrage? Why have you targeted only one community in India? Why does your ‘smashing of patriarchy’ change depending on the religion?” she asked, referring to the Congress government’s decision to overturn the Supreme Court judgment in the Shah Bano case that had granted maintenance to the petitioner.

Ms. Swaraj cited statements by several Congress leaders, alleging that they had made inappropriate remarks against women. She questioned why, if the party genuinely wanted to challenge patriarchy, there was no woman minister in the Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh Cabinets.

The BJP leader also criticised Mr. Gandhi and the Congress for opposing the BJP government’s Triple Talaq legislation. She listed the government’s women-focused policies to emphasise what she described as its record of economic and social empowerment of women.

“So far 95 deaths have been reported,” spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle told AFP, adding that some 28 police personnel were also missing.

World.title: Tension prevails at Nagarjunasagar as A.P. draws water unilaterally, TG retaliates
World.content:
HYDERABAD

Tension prevailed at the Nagarjunasagar dam site in Nalgonda district on Wednesday afternoon as Andhra Pradesh released 2,000 cusecs of water to the Right Canal serving A.P. without any approval of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB), despite objections raised by Telangana.

As the A.P. authorities/engineers were adamant, the Telangana officials too started releasing water to the Left Canal as a move of retaliation. It was only on August 24 that a three-member committee of the river board met here but could not make a decision on sharing and release of water and decided to meet again on September 4.

According to sources in the Telangana Irrigation Department, they were forced to release water to the Left Canal since A.P. authorities released water to the Right Canal unilaterally and illegally, overlooking the objections of Telangana. The instances of high-handedness of the A.P. authorities were umpteen in the past too. As at 9 p.m. on Wednesday, A.P. was drawing 4,050 cusecs for Right Canal and Telangana was drawing 1,580 cusecs for Left Canal.

The Nagarjunasagar reservoir had 181.3 tmc ft of water against its full capacity of 312 tmc ft as on Wednesday evening. The A.P. authorities were also drawing huge quantities of water from Srisailam from Pothireddypadu Head Regulator and Handri-Neeva pumping system to take the water to the outside basin areas, even before the common reservoir became surplus, the sources said.

Meanwhile, the Opposition Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) has taken strong exception to the Congress government’s failure to protect Telangana’s river water interests, particularly in the El Nino year. Former minister for Irrigation and Deputy Floor Leader in the Assembly T. Harish Rao observed that the State government appeared to be powerless before A.P. as it had disregarded KRMB.

“Isn’t it the high-handedness of A.P. officials to draw water without the approval of the KRMB and despite the fact that the project is under the management of Telangana”, Mr. Harish Rao asked. He stated that A.P. had asked for 47 tmc ft water from Nagarjunasagar, and the matter was to be discussed and decided by the three-member committee. He questioned the silence of KRMB and the Telangana government.

He alleged that A.P. was taking 11 tmc ft water from Srisailam through Veligonda project tunnels in addition to drawal from PRP-HR, Handri-Neeva pumping station. He demanded immediate intervention of the KRMB to stop A.P. drawing water illegally and requested Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy to take up the matter with Minister of Jal Shakti immediately.

World.title: A.P. Man held for woman’s death in Saligramam
World.content:
The Greater Chennai Police have arrested a 32-year-old man from Guntur in Andhra Pradesh in connection with the death of a woman from Saligramam after he threatened to share her private videos and photos with her husband on Monday.

Police sources said the 32-year-old victim was staying with her husband and three-year-old son. She was found dead at her house on Monday under suspicious circumstances. The Virugambakkam police took up investigation into the suspicious death and declared it as a case of suicide.

After examining the mobile phone contact details, police found that she was in constant touch with Mohammed Hussain, 32, who ran a travel business in the area, and another man. The police found online transfers through an online money portal from her phone to the two men.

Police said the woman had stopped communicating with the two men in recent days. Following this, the men sent audio recordings and private videos of their conversations to her husband and threatened her.

A team of Virugambakkam police went to Guntur and arrested Mohammed Hussain in connection with the case. He was booked for abetment of suicide. The police are searching for another suspect.

World.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday.

Footage showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area and grief-stricken women sitting on the ground outside the hospital. An AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility.

Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit.

Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged.

However, the hospital disputed this in a statement issued later in the evening. “All emergency exits were fully open and operational,” it asserted.

In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation.

“The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”.

Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said.

Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, who reached Islamabad from Karachi in the afternoon, vowed that “no one responsible for negligence, including me, will be spared”.

“The tragic fire incident at Pims MCH Centre, resulting in the loss of precious neonatal lives, is deeply heartbreaking,” the public hospital said.

Citing a preliminary report, the Pims statement said the incident was “initially caused by a spark inside nursery at 06:38am and within seconds a massive fire erupted due to oxygen points at each incubator”.

It said two doctors and two nurses on duty inside the nursery responded “immediately and called security staff, who joined in and tried to get in twice [to bring] babies out until 06:39am, when a huge blast occurred and ceilings fell down”.

The statement said the duty staff managed to rescue a baby in the nursery and four in an adjacent room, along with three mothers.

“Besides immediate response, staff managed rescue of 73 other admitted patients in the adjacent Gynae ward on the same floor within minutes,” it added.

The hospital asserted that “available fire safety equipment installed, including 35 fire extinguishers, were all utilised by the staff to contain the situation”.

Health minister vows accountability

Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, the health minister said he will present himself to his superiors for accountability.

Providing details of the incident, Kamal said: “At 6:38am, it can be seen in the CCTV footage that there was a spark in the AC, then a fireball could be seen erupting out of it and landing on the floor of the ward. In one minute, at 6:39am, four people, including two nurses and two doctors, could be seen rushing for help and around the same time, the whole room was engulfed in flames”.

The health minister said the incident was being investigated by “experts, different institutions including us”, adding that “nothing will remain hidden and all facts will be unearthed”.

He continued: “Apparently, it seems that 14 out of the 15 infants were connected to oxygen tubes and it was that oxygen which caught flame.”

Kamal reiterated that the “heart-wrenching” incident will be investigated and warned that “if there was any negligence, then as I said, we will not spare them, including myself”.

The minister further said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed him “not to speak about certain issues”. He said he would be meeting the premier and that the two had been in touch.

“Everyone is on board, and the findings will be presented,” he said.

On being asked if he was going to tender his resignation, the health minister said, “As I have said before, whoever is responsible [..] they will not be spared. I have said what I can, and I wish I could say more, but the prime minister is my boss, and whatever his orders will be, I can only say that.”

The federal minister was also questioned about fire safety standards at Pims, with a reporter pointing out that the hospital had been issued notices for the past eight years.

Kamal claimed that the hospital had ensured compliance each time a notice had been issued in the past, pointing out that the blaze was contained with “26 fire extinguishers available in the building”.

When a reporter asked about his early morning statement over the lack of adequate facilities at Pims and “why in his 2-2.5 years as a health minister, no improvement had been made”, the minister, getting visibly frustrated, said, “If it has been 2-2.5 years, then feel free to shoot me” and clarified that he had only been at his position for one year and two months.

“What I said in the morning has to be seen within a certain parameter. I was saying that even if this did not happen, there are still challenges at the hospital. It has a capacity of 200-300 OPDs, and today, it has a footfall of over 9,000 people”.

He maintained that he was merely presenting facts. “I am not saying that everything is ideal.”

When pointed out that it was his responsibility to upgrade the facility, Kamal acknowledged his role and said, “We have to do it, but things cannot be ideal given the current scenario, but if we go into that, the conversation will take a different turn”.

The minister reiterated that every responsible person will be held accountable. “If I am willing to present myself for accountability, then no one else is left.

“Wherever there has been negligence, we will fix it,” he said. Noting that such an incident should not have happened, he said: “Will get to its root cause and ensure prevention in the future.”

The minister was also asked about reports that the door of the ward was locked, to which he said that access to the ward was limited and guarded due to “instances of people stealing newborn babies a couple of years back”.

“You would not see that anywhere else in the world, but we have the issue, so the door had to be manned with a guard,” Kamal explained.

During his media talk, the minister got into a verbal altercation with an individual who asked when action would be taken against those responsible. As the individual got louder, the minister repeatedly gestured to him to come forward and said, “Sir, come here and talk to me.”

‘Give me my child back’

Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing.

“After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said.

A worker removes broken pieces of a glass window after a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — Reuters

Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive.

“I lost my daughter. She was only three days old,” he said. “My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help.”

He added, “The fire erupted at 6am, rescue and authorities reached at 9am; people were helping themselves.”

“Give me my child back,” Jaweria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital. “I want justice.”

She told AFP: “Rescue teams arrived too late. Police arrived after four hours and said they are here to investigate. To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them.”

Jaweria (2nd R), who said she lost her child in the fire, reacts following the blaze at the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP

“For two hours I kept crying and wailing,” the mother said, questioning the action taken by hospital staff and emergency responders.

“Why did the doctors leave the children there? One nurse, one doctor, one gynaecologist, one paediatrician — there was nobody in the entire ward. Why were they not there?”

Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was “no fire security” in the ward.

A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms.

“People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe,” Shagufta Parveen told AFP.

A man consoles a grieving father (C) as his child’s coffin is carried after a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP

Ali Abbas, 20, was with his sister who was a patient in the ward.

“There was a short circuit in the nursery, in the children’s ward,” he said. “It was full of smoke.”

Eyewitness Abdul Ghafoor told AFP that there was “thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped”.

“I barged in to try to save as many people as I could, but we could not reach the ward where the patients were.

“The fire was in the nursing room, and we could not see anything. Some of us broke the windows to help people get out.”

Among the victims were the twin daughters of Bahadur Khan, a vegetable seller, The New York Times reported. He had left them with their mother to get some rest at home. Bahadur said his wife was recovering in Pims’ intensive care unit and was not aware of the deaths of their three-day-old daughters.

Alam Zaib, the father of a newborn child who was in another ward and remained safe, was quoted as saying that he tried to enter the ward where the fire broke out, but the door was locked.

Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes.

Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement.

Federal health secretary removed

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate it. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families.

“Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying.

“The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said.

In a second statement, the PMO said the prime minister had suspended and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri.

The premier chaired a high-level meeting on the incident, where he expressed his anger and issued directives for “strict action”, the PMO said in another statement.

It also stated that the prime minister suspended the federal health secretary and asked him to leave the meeting.

The statement quoted the prime minister as saying: “I am heartbroken at this tragic incident and share the parents’ grief.”

Subsequently, Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood, a BS-21 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was appointed to the post of health secretary for three months “or till the posting of a regular incumbent,” a notification issued by the Cabinet Secretariat said.

According to the PMO, a high-level inquiry committee, headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, has launched an investigation.

State-run APP reported that Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan was also included in the committee.

Further, a notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general (ADCG), had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire.

The members of the committee included the CES director general, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) Electrical and Mechanical wing, along with representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company.

The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations.

The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours.

Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP

Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik assured in a post on X that a “complete, transparent, and impartial investigation of the incident will be conducted to determine the true causes of this catastrophe and any possible negligence”.

“In the event that negligence or failure is proven at any level, strict action will be taken against the responsible individuals in accordance with the law,” he added, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and expressing grief over the incident.

Meanwhile, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari, who reached Pims along with Senator Sherry Rehman and others, demanded that the head of the MCH be removed.

Bokhari said it was not just negligence but rather criminal negligence and should not be ignored.

Rehman said the Pims’ executive director must “answer why the system here keeps being akin to gross negligence”.

“The health ministry now has no justification for taking public funds. It should be dissolved or devolved to the provinces,” she was quoted as saying by her party.

She insisted they were not visiting “to play politics” but were sent by the party leadership to raise questions on behalf of the public.

In a post on her X account, Rehman also shared a video of her visiting the ward.

“Totally gutted. People had to break windows and jump out. Emergency gate was closed, fire equipment not working, medical staff not present,” she wrote.

“Honestly, I would have resigned on the spot,” Rehman added later.

Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration

Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry insisted that there had not been any delay in the arrival of rescue teams and defended the district administration.

“After receiving information in the control room, they reached the hospital within six minutes,” the state minister said while speaking to the media in Islamabad.

He added that once the rescue teams assessed the situation, 19 people were rescued, including seven children, 1o mothers and two men.

He also said that administration officials “from the assistant commissioner to commissioner to the Islamabad IG” reached the hospital to monitor the situation. “Not only did they monitor but also assisted in the rescue operation,” he said.

Reiterating that rescue teams reached the site within six minutes, the state minister said, “There appears to be no negligence on the part of rescue services.”

However, he added, only the hospital administration could answer for the arrangements present within the hospital.

Chaudhry said that the bodies of all 14 infants had been handed over to their families.

He added that a report of the incident had been sent to the prime minister and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who he said had been monitoring the situation.

On being asked if Pims met the CDA’s fire safety protocols, with a journalist also pointing out that his ministry had been issuing notices to the hospital for the past seven years, he acknowledged that notices had been issued.

“It is a huge institution, and notices were issued […] but what was complied with and what was not — as there are multiple buildings; we cannot conclude anything today, and an inquiry committee has been formed”.

Asked why the administration had not been active on the fire safety issue before, he said, “If there has been any negligence, the inquiry committee will find out.”

An inquiry committee has been formed for a “high-powered” investigation into the incident, Chaudhry noted. He said the committee will collect evidence — CCTV footage, presence of flammable equipment, why the door was locked, the number of doctors and nurses present — and present its findings.

In its update on the incident, CDA said fire and rescue teams reached the site within seven minutes after a call was received at 6:54am.

Fire tenders, rescue teams, ambulances of the Capital Emergency Services (CES) and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration were part of the deployed resources.

Nation expresses grief

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”.

“Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said.

Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the incident.

“My deepest condolences to the bereaved parents and families. No words can ease the pain of losing an innocent child. May Allah Almighty grant the families strength and sabr in this unimaginably difficult hour,” he said.

As per the prime minister’s orders an immediate and thorough investigation will establish the causes of this tragic incident to ensure that those found responsible face the strictest action. The safety of our children must remain paramount,” he said.

PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari wrote on X: “Mothers do not keep their children in the womb for nine months just so that, due to someone’s negligence, they burn alive as soon as they are born.

“The deaths of 14 newborns in the federal capital are one of the most horrific tragedies in human history. The helpless fathers, whose lamps of hope were extinguished the very instant they were lit, are seeking justice.”
